segments_en: He was telling stories, saying in his storytelling: Whoever is overtaken by dawn in a state of janābah should not fast.
I mentioned that to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, [that is] to his father, and he rejected it.

So ʿAbd al-Raḥmān went and I went with him until we entered upon ʿĀʾishah and Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with them both). ʿAbd al-Raḥmān asked them about that. He said: Both of them said: The Prophet ﷺ would wake up in the morning in a state of janābah, not from a wet dream, and then fast. He said: Then we went until we entered upon Marwān, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān mentioned that to him.

Marwān said: I adjure you to go to Abū Hurayrah and refute to him what he says. He said: So we came to Abū Hurayrah, and Abū Bakr was present for all of that. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān mentioned it to him, and Abū Hurayrah said: Did the two of them tell you that? He said: Yes.
He said: They know best.
Then Abū Hurayrah attributed what he used to say about that to al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās, and Abū Hurayrah said: I heard that from al-Faḍl, and I did not hear it from the Prophet ﷺ.
He said: So Abū Hurayrah retracted what he used to say about that.
I said to ʿAbd al-Malik: Did they both say it about Ramadan? He said: Yes, he would wake up in a state of janābah, not from a wet dream, and then fast.
error: رددتَ عليه means 'refute/counter what he says', not 'retract'. As written, Marwān seems to ask ʿAbd al-Raḥmān to retract, when he is asking him to refute Abū Hurayrah's position.

segments_en: A woman,
— he said in the hadith of Abān: from Juhaynah — came to the Prophet ﷺ and said that she had committed adultery and was pregnant.
So the Prophet ﷺ summoned her guardian, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Treat her well, and when she gives birth, bring her to me."

When she gave birth, he brought her, and the Prophet ﷺ gave orders concerning her. Her garments were fastened around her, then he ordered that she be stoned, and she was stoned. Then he ordered them and they prayed over her. ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, you pray over her when she has committed adultery?" He said:

"By the One in whose hand is my soul, she has repented with a repentance that, if it were divided among seventy of the people of Medina, it would suffice them. Have you found anything better than that she gave herself up?"
He did not say from Abān, "her garments were fastened around her."
error: Added clause: 'for the sake of Allah' is not in the Arabic (جادت بنفسها means she gave herself/her life).

segments_en: "The people have been neglected,
and you are the son of ʿUmar and a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ. What prevents you from going out?" He said, "What prevents me is that Allah has forbidden the blood of my brother."
They said, "Did Allah not say: {And fight them until there is no more fitnah}?" He said, "We fought until there was no more fitnah,
and the religion was for Allah,
whereas you want to fight until there is fitnah,
and the religion is for other than Allah."
ʿUthmān ibn Ṣāliḥ added, from Ibn Wahb,
who said: So-and-so informed me,
and Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ,
from Bakr ibn ʿAmr al-Maʿāfirī,
that Bukayr ibn ʿAbdullāh
narrated to him from Nāfiʿ that a man
came to Ibn ʿUmar and said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, what makes you perform Hajj one year and ʿUmrah another year,
and abandon jihad in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic,

when you know how much Allah has encouraged it?" He said, "O son of my brother, Islam is built upon five: belief in Allah and His Messenger, the five prayers, fasting Ramadan, paying zakāh, and Hajj to the House."
He said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,

do you not hear what Allah mentions in His Book: {And if two groups of the believers fight each other, make peace between them} {until it returns to the command of Allah} {and fight them until there is no more fitnah}?" He said, "We did that in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when Islam was small in number,
and a man would be persecuted for his religion; they would either kill him or torture him,
until Islam grew, and there was no more fitnah."
He said, "Then what do you say about ʿAlī and ʿUthmān?" He said, "As for ʿUthmān, it is as if Allah pardoned him,
but you disliked to pardon him.
As for ʿAlī, he is the cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his son-in-law."
And he pointed with his hand and said, "That is his house, where you see it."
error: Segment 21: the one who dislikes to pardon is 'you' (تعفوا), not Allah; the translation wrongly makes the pardon Allah's ('that He pardon him').

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. (Transmission switches:) And al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ narrated to us:
Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us:
Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us,
from Thābit al-Bunānī,
from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabāḥ,
from Abū Qatādah:

That the Prophet ﷺ went out one night and found Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, praying with a low voice. He said: And he passed by ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who was praying with a raised voice. He said: When the two were together with the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Abū Bakr, I passed by you while you were praying with your voice lowered." He said:
"I made the One I was whispering to hear me, Messenger of Allah."
He said: And he said to ʿUmar:
"I passed by you while you were praying with your voice raised." He said: ʿUmar said:
"Messenger of Allah, I was waking the drowsy and driving away Satan."
Al-Ḥasan added in his narration: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Abū Bakr, raise your voice a little." And he said to ʿUmar:
"Lower your voice a little."
error: Narrator's name is wrong: the Arabic has ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabāḥ, but the translation omits 'Abī' and gives ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ, a different name.

segments_en: Salmā, a freed slave from the people of Madinah and a truthful man, said: While I was sitting with Abū Hurayrah, a Persian woman came to him with a son of hers, and they both claimed him, her husband having divorced her. She said, "O Abū Hurayrah," and she spoke to him in Persian, "my husband wants to take my son away." Abū Hurayrah said, "Draw lots over him," and he spoke to her in Persian to that effect. Then her husband came and said, "Who disputes with me over my son?" Abū Hurayrah said, "O Allah, I say this only because I heard a woman come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while I was sitting with him, and she said, 'O Messenger of Allah, my husband wants to take my son away, though my son has given me water to drink from the well of Abū ʿInabah and has benefited me.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Draw lots over him."
Her husband said, "Who disputes with me over my son?" The Prophet ﷺ said,
"This is your father and this is your mother, so take the hand of whichever of them you wish."
So he took his mother's hand, and she went away with him.
error: The woman says her son (not her husband) gave her water from the well of Abū ʿInabah and benefited her; the translation makes the husband the one who did this.

segments_en: When Abū Ṭālib was approaching death, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and found with him Abū Jahl and ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Umayyah ibn al-Mughīrah. He said:
"Uncle, say: 'There is no god but Allah,'
a word with which I will plead for you before Allah."
Abū Jahl and ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Umayyah said, "Do you turn away from the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept presenting it to him,
and the two kept repeating that statement to him, until the last thing Abū Ṭālib said to them was that he was on the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib,
and he refused to say, "There is no god but Allah."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By Allah, I will surely ask forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden to do so."
Then Allah revealed: {It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists}, and Allah revealed concerning Abū Ṭālib,
and He said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: {Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills.}
Ibn ʿAbbās said: {Those of strength}: a group of men could not lift it. {Would weigh down}: would burden.
{Empty}: except for the remembrance of Moses. {The exultant}: the boastful.
{Follow him}: follow his trail,
and it can also mean relating a account, as in {We relate to you}.
{From a distance}: from afar; ʿan junub and ʿan janābah are the same,
and also ʿan ijtināb. Yabṭishu and yabṭushu [are both used]. {They are conspiring}: they are consulting one another.
ʿUdwān, ʿadāʾ, and taʿaddī are the same. {I perceived}: I saw.
Al-jadhwah is a thick piece of wood
that has no flame,
whereas a shihāb has a flame.
Snakes are of several kinds: the jānn, vipers, and black snakes. {A helper}: an aid.
Ibn ʿAbbās read {confirm me}. Another said: {We will strengthen}: we will support you; whenever you strengthen something, you have made an arm for it. Maqbūḥīn: destroyed.
{We have connected}: We made it clear and completed it.
{Is brought}: is carried. {Became insolent}: became arrogant.
{In its mother, a messenger}: the Mother of the Towns is Makkah and what surrounds it. {Conceal}: hide.
Aknantu al-shayʾ means I hid it,
and kanantuhu means I hid it and [also] I made it apparent.
{Wayka-nna Allah} is like "Do you not see that Allah {extends provision to whom He wills and restricts}": He gives abundance to him and narrows it for him.
error: Segment 21: 'الْجَانُّ' is a kind of snake, not 'jinn'; the translation wrongly says the snakes are kinds of jinn.

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, meaning on the expedition of Dhāt al-Riqāʿ. A man captured the wife of one of the polytheists, and the polytheist swore that he would not stop until he had shed blood among the Companions of Muḥammad. So he set out following the trail of the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ stopped at a camping place and said, "Who will keep watch for us?" A man from the Muhājirūn and a man from the Anṣār volunteered, and he said:
"Stay at the mouth of the mountain pass."

He said: When the two men went out to the mouth of the pass, the Muhājir lay down and the Anṣārī stood praying. The man came, and when he saw his figure he knew he was a lookout for the people, so he shot him with an arrow and lodged it in him. He pulled it out, until the man had shot him with three arrows. Then he bowed and prostrated. Then his companion woke up, and when the man realized that they had been alerted to him, he fled. When the Muhājir saw the blood on the Anṣārī, he said: Glory be to Allah! Why did you not wake me at the first shot? He said: I was in the middle of a sūrah that I was reciting, and I did not like to cut it short.
error: أصاب امرأة رجل من المشركين means a Muslim man took the polytheist's wife captive, not that he struck her. The translation also leaves unclear who swore the oath, which was the polytheist husband.

segments_en: I entered upon Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, and he said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There will be a trial, division, and disagreement. When that happens, take your sword to Uḥud and strike it until it breaks, then sit in your house until a sinful hand or a decisive death comes to you."
And it has indeed occurred, and I have done what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said.
error: أُحُدًا is the mountain Uḥud, not 'a rock'; the place name was mistranslated.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ordered him to learn the writing of the Jews,
until I wrote letters for the Prophet ﷺ,
and I read their letters to him when they wrote to him.

ʿUmar said, while ʿAlī, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and ʿUthmān were with him, "What does this woman say?" ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥāṭib said, "I said: She is telling you about their companion who did that to the two of them."
Abū Jamrah said, "I used to translate between Ibn ʿAbbās and the people."
And some people said, "A judge must have two translators."
error: Segment 6: مُتَرْجِمَيْنِ is dual, meaning two translators; the translation gave an unspecified plural, which loses the number the statement is about.

segments_en: When we left Makkah, the daughter of Ḥamzah followed us, calling, "O uncle! O uncle!"
ʿAlī took her, held her by the hand, and said, "Take your cousin's daughter."
So she (Fāṭimah) carried her. Then he related the report. He said: Jaʿfar said, "She is my cousin's daughter, and her maternal aunt is my wife."
The Prophet ﷺ ruled that she go to her maternal aunt, and he said,
"The maternal aunt is in the position of the mother."
error: فَحَمَلَتْهَا is third-person feminine (Fāṭimah carried her), not 'I carried her'; the wrong subject was given.

segments_en: Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl went out to Syria,
asking about the religion so that he might follow it. He met a scholar of the Jews,
and asked him about their religion,
and said, "Perhaps I will adopt your religion, so tell me about it."
He said, "You will not be on our religion until you take your share of the anger of Allah."
Zayd said, "I flee only from the anger of Allah,
and I will never bear any of the anger of Allah,
and how could I bear it? Can you guide me to something other than this?" He said, "I know of nothing except that he be a ḥanīf."
Zayd said, "What is a ḥanīf?" He said, "The religion of Ibrāhīm, who was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and worshipped none but Allah."
So Zayd left and met a scholar of the Christians, and mentioned the same to him,
and he said, "You will not be on our religion until you take your share of the curse of Allah."
He said, "I flee only from the curse of Allah,
and I will never bear any of the curse of Allah nor of His anger,
and how could I bear it? Can you guide me to something other than this?" He said, "I know of nothing except that he be a ḥanīf."
He said, "What is a ḥanīf?" He said, "The religion of Ibrāhīm, who was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and worshipped none but Allah."
When Zayd saw what they said about Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, he left,
and when he came out into the open, he raised his hands and said, "O Allah, I bear witness that I am on the religion of Ibrāhīm."
error: "وَأَنَّى أَسْتَطِيعُهُ" is a rhetorical question ("how could I bear it?"). The translation instead has Zayd claiming he is able to avoid it, which reverses the sense. This occurs in segments 8 and 14.

segments_en: May Allah have mercy on Ibrāhīm. People were strict about nabīdh, but he granted a concession regarding it.
error: Wrong subject. In the Arabic, the people were strict about nabīdh and Ibrāhīm permitted it. The translation makes Ibrāhīm the one who was strict with people.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The likeness of the one who is lax regarding the limits of Allah and the one who falls into violating them is that of a people who cast lots for a ship,
so some of them ended up on its lower deck and some on its upper deck.
Those on the lower deck would pass by those on the upper deck to get water, and this bothered them, so one of them took an axe
and began to strike at the bottom of the ship.
They came to him and said, 'What is the matter with you?' He said, 'You were bothered by me,
and I must have water.'
If they take hold of his hands, they will save him and save themselves,
but if they leave him, they will destroy him and destroy themselves."
error: المدهن (one who is lax or compromises regarding Allah's limits) was mistranslated as "one who observes the limits of Allah", which reverses the meaning of the comparison.

segments_en: That a governor
in Mecca used to give the salām twice, so ʿAbdullāh said, "Where did he pick that up from?" Al-Ḥakam said in his narration that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do it.
error: أَنَّى عَلِقَهَا means "where did he get/learn it from?", a rhetorical question of disapproval. The translation turns it into an affirmation that he had truly learned it.

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, he gathered the women of the Anṣār in a house and sent ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to us. He stood at the door and greeted us with salām, and we returned the greeting. Then he said: I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to you.

He commanded us to bring out, for the two Eids, the menstruating women and the adolescent girls, [and said] that Friday prayer is not obligatory on us, and he forbade us from following funeral processions.
error: الْعُتَّقَ (al-ʿutuq, i.e. al-ʿawātiq) means young, adolescent girls, not slave girls; the mistranslation changes who is commanded to go out.

segments_en: He heard the Prophet ﷺ say that his Basin is [as wide as] the distance between Ṣanʿāʾ and Medina.
Al-Mustawrid said to him: "Did you not hear him mention the vessels?" He said: "No."
Al-Mustawrid said: "You will see in it vessels like the stars."
error: Wrong subject in segment 1: the narrator heard the Prophet ﷺ speak. The English says the Prophet ﷺ heard the statement.

segments_en: He had gone blind, so he sent for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Come and mark out a place of prayer for me."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, and his people came, and a man among them called Mālik ibn al-Dukhshum was described.
Then he mentioned a hadith similar to the hadith of Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah.
error: Segment 1 wrongly says "He is my uncle"; the Arabic says he had gone blind (أَنَّهُ عَمِيَ).

segments_en: The people of the Ṣuffah
were poor people, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ once said: "
Whoever has food for two should take a third with him, and whoever has food for four should take a fifth, or a sixth."
Or as he said.

Abū Bakr came with three, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ went with ten, and Abū Bakr with three. He said: So it was he, I, my father, and my mother, and I do not know whether he said, "and my wife," and a servant shared between our house and the house of Abū Bakr. He said: Abū Bakr dined with the Prophet ﷺ.

Then he stayed until the night prayer was prayed, then he returned and stayed until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became drowsy. Then he came after a portion of the night had passed, as Allah willed. His wife said to him: What kept you from your guests? Or she said: your guest. He said: Did you not feed them dinner? She said: They refused until you came. They had offered it to them, but they had overpowered them. He said: So I went and hid, and he said: O Ghunthar!
He cut me off and cursed me, and said: Eat, may it not be pleasant for you!

And he said: By Allah, I will never eat it. He said: By Allah, we did not take a morsel but that more grew from beneath it. He said: Until we were full, and it became more than it had been before. Abū Bakr looked at it, and it was just as it was or more.

He said to his wife: O sister of Banū Firās, what is this? She said: No, by the delight of my eye, it is now three times more than it was before. He said: Then Abū Bakr ate from it and said: That was only from Satan, meaning his oath. Then he ate a morsel from it, then carried it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it remained with him until morning. He said: There was a treaty between us and a certain people, and its term expired. We identified twelve men, with each man were people; Allah knows how many with each man, except that he sent them along with them. And they all ate from it.
Or as he said.
error: Segment 6: 'until I had prayed the night prayer' wrongly makes the narrator the one who prayed; the Arabic is passive: 'until the night prayer was prayed'.

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
Like the hadith of Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, except that Ibn Ayyūb said in his narration, "like His permission."
error: كَإِذْنِهِ means "like his/His permission" (idhn), not "ear" (udhn); the translation gives the wrong word and changes the sense.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill, so we prayed behind him while he was sitting, and Abū Bakr was calling out the takbīr so that the people could hear his takbīr. He turned to us and saw us standing, so he gestured to us and we sat, and we prayed following his prayer, sitting. When he finished the prayer with the salām, he said:

"You were just now doing what the Persians and the Romans do, standing over their kings while they are seated. Do not do so. Follow your imams: if he prays standing, pray standing, and if he prays sitting, pray sitting."
error: "آنفًا تفعلون" means they were just now doing it, not "about to do"; the translation changes a completed act into an intended one.

segments_en: Yaḥyā said: I have not met a man among us resembling him, narrating to the people that Saʿd ibn Zurārah, who was the maternal grandfather of Muḥammad, was seized by a pain in his throat called the diphtheria, so the Prophet ﷺ said: "
I will certainly try, or I will certainly test [myself], to excuse myself regarding Abū Umāmah."
So he cauterized him with his own hand, and he died. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
What a bad death for the Jews! They say: Why did he not ward it off from his companion?
And I have no power to do anything for him, nor for myself."
error: In segment 4 the bad death (مِيتَةَ سُوءٍ) is said for the Jews, not for Saʿd. The translation wrongly gives "[Saʿd]" as the one it is said for.

segments_en: Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah came and placed his hand on my shoulder,
and I went with him to Saʿd. Then Abū Rāfiʿ said to al-Miswar, "Will you not instruct this man to buy my house that is in my compound from me?"
[Saʿd] said, "I will not add to four hundred,
either in installments or in parts."
[Abū Rāfiʿ] said, "I was offered five hundred in cash, and I refused it.
Had I not heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'The neighbor has more right to what is next to him,'
I would not have sold it to you," or he said, "I would not have given it to you."
I said to Sufyān, "Maʿmar did not say it this way."
He said, "But he said it to me this way."

Some people said: If someone wishes to sell [property subject to] preemption (shufʿah), he may devise a stratagem to nullify the right of preemption: the seller gives the house to the buyer as a gift,
defines its boundaries and hands it over to him,
and the buyer compensates him with a thousand dirhams,
so that the preemptor has no right of preemption over it.
error: Segment 2: دَارِي means "my compound", but the translation says "your compound".

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he came to the graveyard and greeted its inhabitants, saying:
"Peace be upon you, abode of believing people. And we, if Allah the Exalted wills, will be joining you." Then he said:
"I wish that we had seen our brothers."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, are we not your brothers?" He said:
"You are my Companions, and my brothers are those who will come after me, and I will precede you to the Basin."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize those of your nation who have not yet come?" He said:
"Do you not see that if a man had horses with white foreheads and white legs among horses that were pure black, would he not recognize them?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"They will come on the Day of Resurrection with bright faces and limbs from the traces of ablution." He said:
"I will precede them to the Basin."
Then he said, "Beware! Some men will be driven away from my Basin as a stray camel is driven away. I will call to them, 'Come here!'
It will be said, 'They changed [things] after you, and they kept turning back on their heels.'
So I will say, 'Away with them! Away with them!'"
error: Segment 5: the Prophet says 'my brothers' (إخواني) are those who come after him, not 'our brothers'.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is a man whose face Allah turned away from the Fire, toward Paradise, and a shady tree was shown to him. He said: 'My Lord, bring me forward to this tree so that I may be in its shade.'"
And he narrated the hadith like the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd, but did not mention:
"He will say: 'O son of Adam, what will put an end to your asking Me?'"
up to the end of the hadith, and he added in it:

"And Allah will remind him: 'Ask for such and such,' until, when his wishes run out, Allah will say: 'It is yours, and ten times its like.'" He said: "Then he will enter his house, and his two wives from among the ḥūr al-ʿīn will come in to him and say: 'Praise be to Allah, who has given you life for us and given us life for you.'" He said: "He will say: 'No one has been given the like of what I have been given.'"
error: قِبَلَ الْجَنَّةِ means 'toward Paradise' (his face turned from the Fire toward Paradise); 'before Paradise' misstates the direction.

segments_en: The brother of ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ gave him fifteen ṣāʿs of barley to feed sixty poor people.
error: The Arabic has "the brother of ʿUbādah" (an iḍāfah), but the English says "My brother ʿUbādah", which changes the identity of the person.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in the heavens will be merciful to you. The womb is a branch from the Most Merciful; whoever maintains it, Allah will maintain him, and whoever severs it, Allah will sever him."
error: مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ means "the One in the heavens" (or "He who is in heaven"); "above the heavens" changes the wording and the stated fact.

segments_en: I asked Umm Salamah how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite this verse: {Indeed, it is a deed that is not righteous}. She said, "He recited it: {Indeed, he did other than righteous}." Abū Dāwūd said: Hārūn al-Naḥwī and Mūsā ibn Khalaf also narrated it from Thābit as ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said.
error: The variant reading was rendered identically to the first reading. 'ʿamila ghayra ṣāliḥ' means 'he did other than righteous', not 'it is a deed that is not righteous'.

segments_en: I had sheep at Uḥud, and death befell them. So I went to Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and mentioned that to her. Maymūnah said to me, "If only you had taken their hides and benefited from them."
I said, "Is that permissible?" She said, "Yes.
Some men of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dragging a sheep of theirs, [bloated] like a donkey. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them,
'If only you had taken its hide.'
They said, 'It is carrion.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
'Water and qaraẓ [acacia pods] purify it.'"
error: Wrong speaker in segment 2: the Arabic is feminine and the narrator is a woman, so it should be 'I said', not 'He said'.

segments_en: Give glad tidings to those who walk through the darkness to the mosques of perfect light on the Day of Resurrection."
error: The Arabic says those who walk in the darkness to the mosques will be given perfect light on the Day of Resurrection. The English wrongly renders it as 'in the darkness of the perfect light', which changes who has the light and when.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Abraham, peace be upon him, migrated with Sarah,
and entered a town in which there was a king among the kings,
or a tyrant among the tyrants.
It was said: Abraham has entered with a woman
who is among the most beautiful of women.
So he sent for him: O Abraham,
who is this woman with you? He said: My sister.
Then he returned to her
and said: Do not give the lie to my statement, for I told them that you are my sister,
and by Allah, there is no believer on the earth other than you and me.
So he sent her to him, and he got up to approach her,
and she got up to perform ablution and pray. She said: O Allah, if I have believed in You and in Your messenger, and have guarded my chastity
except from my husband, then do not give this disbeliever power over me.
So he was choked until he kicked the ground with his foot."
Al-Aʿraj said: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said that Abū Hurayrah said: She said: O Allah, if he dies, it will be said that she killed him.
So he released her, then got up to approach her again.
She got up to perform ablution and pray,
and she said: O Allah, if I have believed in You and in Your messenger, and have guarded my chastity
except from my husband,
then do not give this disbeliever power over me.
So he was choked until he kicked the ground with his foot.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Abū Salamah said: Abū Hurayrah said: She said: O Allah, if he dies, it will be said that she killed him.
So he released her the second time,
or the third,
and said: By Allah, you have sent me only a devil.
Return her to Abraham, and give her Hājar.
So she returned to Abraham, peace be upon him, and said: Did you know that Allah has humbled the disbeliever and given a servant girl for service?"
error: Segment 27: آجَرَ is the name Hājar (Hagar), whom the king gave her; it was mistranslated as "a gift".

segments_en: And I met him
in Kufa. He came to Ibn Shubrumah and said, "Bring me in to ʿĪsā so that I may admonish him."
It was as if Ibn Shubrumah feared for him, so he did not do it.
error: Wrong subject and object: the man came to Ibn Shubrumah and asked him to be brought in to ʿĪsā. Ibn Shubrumah did not come to the narrator.

segments_en: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ, "If only you would go to ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy."
So the Prophet ﷺ went to him, riding a donkey,
and the Muslims went walking with him,
over land that was salty and barren.
When the Prophet ﷺ came to him, ʿAbdullāh said, "Keep away from me,
for by Allah, the stench of your donkey has harmed me."
A man from the Anṣār among them said, "By Allah, the donkey of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smells better than you."
A man from ʿAbdullāh's people became angry on his behalf, and the two men insulted each other,
and the companions of each of them became angry for him,
and there was fighting between them with palm branches, hands, and sandals.
It reached us that this verse was revealed: {And if two groups of the believers fight each other, make peace between them.}
error: Wrong speaker in segments 5-6: it was ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy who said "Keep away from me... the stench of your donkey has harmed me," not the Prophet ﷺ.

segments_en: That a Bedouin,
called Abū Thaʿlabah, said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have trained hunting dogs, so give me a ruling about their catch." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"If you have trained dogs, then eat of what they catch for you."
He said: "Whether slaughtered or not slaughtered?" He said: "Yes."
He said: "Even if it has eaten of it?" He said:
"Even if it has eaten of it."
Then he said: "O Messenger of Allah, give me a ruling about my bow." He said:
"Eat whatever your bow brings back to you." He said:
"Whether slaughtered or not slaughtered?"
He said: "Even if it disappears from me?" He said:
"Even if it disappears from you, so long as it does not rot or you find on it a mark other than your arrow."
He said: "Give me a ruling about the vessels of the Magians, if we are forced to use them." He said:
"Wash them and eat from them."
error: Segment 11 reverses the condition: the Arabic says you must not find a mark other than your arrow on the game, but the translation says 'you find no mark on it other than your arrow'.

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd
Allāh ibn Numayr, the wording being Zuhayr's, said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Anas,

who said: The Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah when I was ten years old, and he died when I was twenty. My mothers used to urge me to serve him. He came into our house, and we milked for him from a domestic sheep, and water from the well in the house was mixed with it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank. Then ʿUmar said to him, with Abū Bakr on his left: "O Messenger of Allah, give it to Abū Bakr."
But he gave it to a Bedouin on his right, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one on the right, then the one on the right."
error: Only Abū Bakr was on the Prophet's left; ʿUmar was the speaker who addressed him. The translation puts both ʿUmar and Abū Bakr on his left.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ measured out a span of her waist wrapper for Fāṭimah.
error: The Arabic نِطَاقِهَا means 'her' waist wrapper, not the Prophet's ('his'). This misattributes whose garment it was.

segments_en: Ibn Abī ʿUmar [narrated] to us: Sufyān narrated to us, from az-Zuhrī,
from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū
Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: The son of Ādam harms Me by cursing time, while I am Time; I alternate the night and the day."
error: The English adds the clause "in My hand is the command", which is not in the Arabic text.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"The angels received the soul of a man from those before you. They said: 'Did you do any good?' He said: 'I used to instruct my servants to grant respite and to overlook [the debts of] the well-off.' Allah said: 'Then overlook him.'"
And Abū Mālik reported from Ribʿī:
"I used to make things easy for the well-off and give respite to the one in hardship."
error: فَتَجَاوَزُوا عَنْهُ is an imperative ('Overlook him'), a command addressed to the angels. The translation made it a past-tense report that the angels overlooked his faults.

segments_en: A Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [reported] that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated, he would hold his upper arms away from his sides until we felt pity for him.
error: The phrase 'حَتَّى نَأْوِيَ لَهُ' means 'until we felt compassion for him'. The translation invents 'until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen', which is a different meaning.

segments_en: A man
came to Sahl ibn Saʿd and said: "So-and-so," referring to the governor of Medina, "curses ʿAlī at the pulpit."
He said: "What does he say?" He said: "He calls him Abū Turāb."
Sahl laughed and said: "By Allah, no one gave him that name except the Prophet ﷺ,
and he had no name more beloved to him than it."
So I asked Sahl to tell me the story,
and I said: "O Abū ʿAbbās, how was it?" He said: ʿAlī came in to Fāṭimah, then went out and lay down in the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Where is your cousin?"
She said: "In the mosque."
So he went out to him and found that his cloak had fallen from his back
and dust had reached his back,
and he began wiping the dust from his back, saying: "
Sit up, O Abū Turāb!" twice.
error: اجْلِسْ means 'sit up/sit', not 'Get up'; the command was mistranslated.

segments_en: The brother of Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from al-Raqāshī,
from Anas ibn Mālik,
who said: When a matter distressed the Prophet ﷺ, he would say:
"O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, in Your mercy I seek relief."
And with this chain he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Persist in saying: 'O Possessor of Majesty and Honor.'"
error: The Arabic says "the brother of Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiyah", not "my brother Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiyah". The translation wrongly makes Zuhayr the narrator's brother and the narrator.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A woman was punished because of a cat that she had confined
until it died of hunger,
and because of it she entered the Fire. [He said, and Allah knows best:] 'You did not feed it or give it water when you confined it,
and you did not release it so that it could eat from the vermin of the earth.'"
error: The words "You did not feed it..." are said by Allah (to the woman). The translation's "It was said" loses the speaker and attribution.

segments_en: His name is Ḥumayd ibn Hāniʾ al-Khawlānī, from Abū ʿAlī al-Janbī,
from Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The rider should greet the one walking, the one walking should greet the one standing, and the few should greet the many."
error: القائم means 'the one standing', not 'the one sitting'; the translation changes who is greeted.

segments_en: He only said, "Shall I enter, all of me?"
because of the smallness of the tent.
error: The words "all of me" are the narrator's question (أَدْخُلُ كُلِّي, "shall I enter all of me?"), not the Prophet's command "Come in, all of you". The translation attributes the wrong statement to the wrong speaker.

segments_en: Her paternal uncle said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you is fasting, let him break his fast with dates; if he does not find dates, then with water, for water is purifying."
error: عمها means "her paternal uncle", not "his paternal aunt". The translation has the wrong relative and the wrong gender.

segments_en: I and the Messenger of Allah
ﷺ, Abū al-Qāsim, used to lie in a single garment while I was menstruating,

in my period. If any of it from me touched him, he would wash the part it touched and not go beyond it to anywhere else, and he would pray in it. Then he would return to me, and if any of it from me touched him, he would do the same, not going beyond it to anywhere else.
error: Segment 2 contains the translation of segment 3, which is then repeated in segment 3. The clauses about washing the affected spot and praying in it are duplicated, and the segments do not correspond to the Arabic.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered us to kill dogs, until a woman would come from the desert with her dog and we would kill it. Then the Prophet ﷺ forbade killing them and said:
"Kill the pure black one with two spots, for it is a devil."
error: عَلَيْكُمْ بِالأَسْوَدِ here means to go after and kill the black dog with two spots. 'Stick to' wrongly suggests keeping it or sparing it, which reverses the sense.

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the funeral of a man from the Ansār,
and we came to the grave before the niche had been dug.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat down and we sat around him, as though birds were perched on our heads.
In his hand was a stick with which he was scratching the ground.
Then he raised his head and said:
"Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the grave."
Two or three times. (In the narration of Jarīr there is an addition here:) And he said:
"Indeed, he hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away and leave, when it is said to him:
'O you, who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your prophet?'"
Hannād said: He said:
"Two angels come to him, make him sit up, and say to him:
'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'My Lord is Allah.' They say to him:
'What is your religion?' He says: 'My religion is Islam.' They say to him:
'What do you say about this man who was sent among you?' He said: He says:
'He is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' They say:
'And how do you know?' He says:
'I read the Book of Allah, believed in it, and held it to be true.'"
In the narration of Jarīr there is an addition:
"That is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: {Allah keeps firm those who believe}." [to the end of] the verse.
Then the two narrators agree. He said:
"Then a caller calls from the heaven:
'My servant has spoken the truth, so spread out a bed for him from Paradise,
open for him a door to Paradise, and clothe him from Paradise.'" He said:
"Then some of its breeze and fragrance comes to him." He said:
"And it is opened for him therein as far as his sight reaches." He said: "And as for the disbeliever..."
and he mentioned his death. He said:
"His soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him, make him sit up, and say:
'Who is your Lord?' He says:
'Hah, hah, hah, I do not know.' They say to him:
'What is your religion?' He says:
'Hah, hah, I do not know.' They say:
'What do you say about this man who was sent among you?' He says:
'Hah, hah, I do not know.'
Then a caller calls from the heaven:
'He has lied, so spread out a bed for him from the Fire, clothe him from the Fire,
and open for him a door to the Fire.'" He said:
"Then some of its heat and scorching wind comes to him." He said:
"And his grave is constricted upon him until his ribs are pressed together."
In the narration of Jarīr there is an addition. He said:
"Then there is appointed over him one who is blind and mute, with a mace of iron,
such that if a mountain were struck with it, it would become dust." He said:
"He strikes him with it a blow that is heard by everything between the east and the west except the two weighty creations [jinn and mankind], and he becomes dust." He said:
"Then the soul is returned to him."
error: Segment 25: the Arabic says a door is opened for him 'therein' (in Paradise) as far as his sight reaches. The translation wrongly says his grave is made spacious.

segments_en: A Jew had a claim of dates against my father, who was killed on the day of Uhud, leaving two orchards. The dates owed to the Jew would consume what was in the two orchards. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Would you take half this year and defer half?"
The Jew refused. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Would you take the harvest [as it is cut]?"

He said: "Inform me." So I informed him, and he came, along with Abū Bakr, and the dates were cut and measured from the base of the palms while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for blessing, until we paid him his full right from the smaller of the two orchards, as ʿAmmār reckoned. Then I brought them fresh dates and water, and they ate and drank. Then he said:
"This is part of the bounty about which you will be asked."
error: فَآذِنِّي فَآذَنْتُهُ means the Prophet ﷺ said "Inform me" and I informed him. The translation wrongly has someone giving permission and the narrator giving leave.

segments_en: Camels became scarce in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he commanded them to slaughter cattle.
error: Omits that camels became scarce (قَلَّتِ), so the sense is lost; adds an unsupported "I said"; omits the connecting "so" (فَ).

segments_en: that he
was sitting working in the market when a woman carrying a baby passed by, and the people stirred up around her, and I stirred with those who stirred. I reached the Prophet ﷺ as he was saying,
"Who is the father of this [child] with you?"
She remained silent, and a young man beside her said, "I am his father, Messenger of Allah."
Then [the Prophet ﷺ] turned to her and said,
"Who is the father of this [child] with you?"
The young man said, "I am his father, Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at some of those around him, asking them about him, and they said, "We know nothing about him except good."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Are you married?" He said, "Yes."
So he ordered that he be stoned, and he was stoned.

He said: We took him out and dug a pit for him as far as we could, then we threw stones at him until he was still. Then a man came asking about the one who had been stoned, so we took him to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "This man has come asking about the wicked one."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"He is indeed better in the sight of Allah than the fragrance of musk."
It turned out that he was his father, and we helped him with washing him, shrouding him, and burying him. I do not know whether he also mentioned praying over him or not.
This is the narration of ʿAbdah, and it is more complete.
error: Wrong subject in segment 14: 'فَأَعَنَّاهُ' means 'we helped him' (the narrator and the others helped the father), not the Prophet ﷺ.

segments_en: ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, asked them about the saying of the Exalted, "When the help of Allah and the conquest come." They said, "The conquest of the cities and the palaces." He said, "What do you say, Ibn ʿAbbās?" He said, "It is an appointed term, or a parable set forth for Muḥammad ﷺ, in which his own death was announced to him."
error: أَجَلٌ means 'appointed term (of death)', not the affirmation 'Indeed'. 'Or rather' also changes the sense of أَوْ ('or').

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Jibrīl in a garment of brocade, filling what is between the heaven and the earth.
error: The English adds 'green', which is not in the Arabic (حُلَّةٍ مِنْ رَفْرَفٍ).

segments_en: We conquered Makkah, and then we went on the expedition to Ḥunayn. The polytheists came in the best battle lines I have ever seen. He said: The cavalry formed ranks, then the fighters, then the women behind them, then the sheep, then the camels. He said: We were a great number, we had reached six thousand, and on the flank of our cavalry was Khālid ibn al-Walīd. He said: Our horses began to turn back behind us, and it was not long before our cavalry broke apart and the Bedouins and those of the people we knew fled. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out:
"O Emigrants! O Emigrants!" Then he said:
"O Helpers! O Helpers!"
He said: Anas said: This is a hadith of confusion (ʿimmiyyah).

He said: We said, "At your service, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ advanced. He said: By Allah, we had barely reached them when Allah defeated them. He said: We took that wealth, then we set out for Ṭāʾif and besieged them for forty nights, then we returned to Makkah and camped. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began giving a man a hundred camels.
Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith like the hadith of Qatādah, Abū al-Tayyāḥ and Hishām ibn Zayd.
error: Segment 4: 'ʿimmiyyah' means confusion or blindness (an obscure, chaotic event), not 'my paternal uncles'.

segments_en: Juwayriyah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to see her and said:
"Is there any food?"
She said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we have no food except a bone from a sheep that was given as charity to my freed slave woman." He said:
"Bring it near, for it has reached its place."
error: Wrong agent: the bone was given to her freed slave woman as charity (passive), not given by the speaker.

segments_en: I went to aṭ-Ṭūr and met Kaʿb there. I stayed with him for a day, telling him about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he told me about the Torah. I said to him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was brought down to earth, on it his repentance was accepted, on it he died, and on it the Hour will come. There is no creature on earth that does not wait attentively on Friday morning until the sun rises, in fear of the Hour, except the son of Adam (mankind). And on it there is an hour which a believer does not happen to meet while he is praying and asking Allah for something, except that He gives it to him."
Kaʿb said: That is one day in every year.
I said: Rather, it is every Friday.
Kaʿb read the Torah and then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke the truth; it is on every Friday.
Then I went out and met Baṣrah ibn Abī Baṣrah al-Ghifārī, who said: Where have you come from? I said: From aṭ-Ṭūr.
He said: If I had met you before you went there, you would not have gone.
I asked him: Why? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Saddle animals are not to be set out except for three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, my mosque, and the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis."

Then I met ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and said: If only you had seen me. I went out to aṭ-Ṭūr and met Kaʿb, and I stayed with him for a day, telling him about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he told me about the Torah. I said to him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was brought down to earth, on it his repentance was accepted, on it he died, and on it the Hour will come. There is no creature on earth that does not wait attentively on Friday morning until the sun rises, in fear of the Hour, except the son of Adam (mankind). And on it there is an hour which a believing servant does not happen to meet while he is praying and asking Allah for something, except that He gives it to him."
Kaʿb said: That is one day in every year.
ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām said: Kaʿb lied.
I said: Then Kaʿb read [the Torah] and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke the truth; it is on every Friday.
ʿAbdullāh said: Kaʿb is right. I know that hour. I said: My brother, tell me about it.
He said: It is the last hour of Friday before the sun sets. I said: Have you not heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
A believer does not happen to meet it while he is praying"?
But that hour is not a time of prayer. He said: Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Whoever prays and then sits waiting for the prayer remains in prayer until the prayer comes to him that he is waiting for"? I said: Yes.
He said: Then it is just so.
error: Added "jinn" (Arabic only says إلا ابن آدم, except the son of Adam/mankind) in segments 2 and 11; in segment 16 "I said: Did I not hear" wrongly makes the speaker the questioner, whereas the Arabic is "Have you not heard" addressed to ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām.

segments_en: I witnessed Marwān ask Abū Hurayrah, "How did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray over a funeral?" He said, "Is it with what you said [before]?" He said, "Yes."
He said: There had been some words between them before that.
Abū Hurayrah said,
"O Allah, You are its Lord, You created it, You guided it to Islam, and You took its soul. You know best its secret and its open [state]. We have come to You as intercessors, so forgive him."
error: Abū Hurayrah's question refers to what Marwān said (قُلْتَ, 'you said'), not what Abū Hurayrah said. The translation wrongly has 'what I said'.

segments_en: Some guests of ours stayed with us. He said:
Abū Bakr used to talk with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at night, and he said:
I will not return to you until you have finished entertaining these guests and serving them. So he brought them their meal, but they said:
We will not eat until Abū Bakr comes. Then he came and said:
What have your guests done? Have you finished serving them? They said: No. I said:
I brought them their meal, but they refused and said:
By Allah, we will not eat it until he comes. Then they said:
He is right; he brought it to us, but we refused until you came. He said:
What stopped you? They said: Your absence. He said:
By Allah, I will not eat it tonight. Then they said:
And by Allah, we will not eat it until you eat. He said:
I have never seen evil like tonight. He said: Bring your food. He said:
So their food was brought near, and he said:
In the name of Allah. He ate and they ate. Then I was told that he went in the morning to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what he had done and what they had done. He said:
"Rather, you are the most dutiful of them and the most truthful of them."
error: Segment 7: 'لاَ نَطْعَمُهُ' means 'we will not eat it', not 'we will not feed him'; the guests refused to eat the food.

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ — or he said: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ —: "
If the Anṣār were to take a valley or a mountain pass,
I would take the valley of the Anṣār,
and were it not for the Hijrah, I would be a man from the Anṣār."
Abū Hurayrah said: "He did not wrong them, by my father and mother! They gave him refuge and they supported him."
Or another statement.
error: ظَلَمَ is active: the Prophet did not wrong the Anṣār. The translation made it passive ("He was not wronged"), which reverses who did what to whom.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me to recite: {Indeed, I am the Provider, the Possessor of power, the Firm.}
error: The Arabic reads 'innī anā al-razzāq' (Indeed, I am the Provider), a first-person variant. The English changed it to 'it is Allah who is the Provider', which alters the recited wording.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered upon a Bedouin to visit him when he was sick. He said: Whenever the Prophet ﷺ visited a sick person, he would say: "No harm, it is a purification, if Allah wills." So he said to him:
"No harm, it is a purification, if Allah wills."
He said: You said, "Purification?" Never! Rather it is a fever boiling," or "erupting, in an old man, that will bring him to the graves." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Then so be it."
error: Wrong speaker: the Bedouin says 'You said (qulta) purification', addressing the Prophet ﷺ; the translation has 'I said'.

segments_en: [He] said, may Allah be pleased with him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Nothing afflicts a believer, whether fatigue, grief, illness, or even worry that concerns him, except that Allah expiates his sins by it."
error: The translation adds "some of" before "his sins". The Arabic says Allah expiates "his sins" (سيئاته), with no limiting qualifier.

segments_en: People say that Ibn ʿUmar
accepted Islam before ʿUmar, but that is not so.
Rather, on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah ʿUmar sent ʿAbdullāh to fetch a horse of his that was with a man of the Anṣār, so that he could fight on it,
while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking pledges at the tree,
and ʿUmar did not know of that.
So ʿAbdullāh gave his pledge,
then went to the horse
and brought it to ʿUmar,
while ʿUmar was putting on his armor for battle.
He told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking pledges under the tree. He said: So he set out and went with him until he gave his pledge to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
That is what people mean when they say that Ibn ʿUmar accepted Islam before ʿUmar.
error: Segment 10 adds a quotation "Let us go" that is not in the Arabic; "قَالَ" is only the narrator's interjection, and the report is that ʿUmar set out with him.

segments_en: For by Allah's permission it is a protection for you. Then know that people have never invented an innovation except that, before it, there had already passed something that is evidence against it or a lesson concerning it. For the Sunnah was only established by one who knew what lies in opposing it. Ibn Kathīr did not say "who knew".

of error, slipping, foolishness, and excessive probing. So be content for yourself with what the people [of the earlier generations] were content with for themselves, for they stopped with knowledge and held back with penetrating insight. They were stronger at uncovering matters, and more deserving of any merit that was in them. If the guidance is what you are following, then you have outstripped them to it. And if you say, "It only arose after them,"

then none introduced it except one who followed a path other than theirs and turned away from them in preference for himself, for they were the forerunners. They spoke about it with what suffices and described of it what heals. So there is none below them who falls short, and none above them who goes beyond. A people fell short of them and so were harsh, and others aspired beyond them and so were excessive, while they were between these two, upon straight guidance. You wrote asking about affirming the decree (qadar); you have fallen upon one well-informed, by Allah's permission. I know of no novelty that people have introduced, nor any innovation they have invented, whose trace is clearer or whose matter is more firmly established than the affirmation of the decree. It was mentioned even in the Days of Ignorance; they spoke of it in their speech and in their poetry, consoling themselves with it over what they had missed. Then Islam added nothing to it except strength. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned it in more than one or two hadith, and the Muslims heard it from him and spoke of it during his life and after his death, in certainty and submission to their Lord, and in acknowledgment of their own weakness, [rejecting the notion] that anything could exist that His knowledge had not encompassed, His Book had not enumerated, and His decree had not carried out. Moreover, it is in the firmly established verses of His Book; from it they took it and from it they learned it. And if you say, "Why did Allah reveal such-and-such verse, and why did He say such-and-such?"

they recited of it what you recite, and they knew of its interpretation what you do not know. After all that they said: it is by a Book and a decree; wretchedness has been written; whatever is decreed will be; what Allah wills is, and what He does not will is not; and we possess for ourselves neither harm nor benefit. Then after that they strove in hope and in fear.
error: Segment 3 reverses the sense: they considered themselves too weak to imagine that anything could exist outside Allah's knowledge, Book and decree. The translation says they believed such a thing could exist.

segments_en: From a written note that he showed me in comparison, then he read it to me; he said: Ḥanẓalah ibn Abī Sufyān informed us: Saʿīd ibn Mīnāʾ narrated to us, saying: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh say: When the trench was being dug, I saw that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in severe hunger, so I turned back to my wife and said to her, "Do you have anything? For I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in severe hunger."

She brought out a bag for me containing a ṣāʿ of barley, and we had a tame young goat. He said: I slaughtered it, and she ground the barley. When I had finished, I cut it up into pieces in her cooking pot. Then I turned to go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said, "Do not disgrace me before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those with him." He said: I came to him and spoke to him privately, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, we have slaughtered a young goat of ours and ground a ṣāʿ of barley that we had, so come, you and a small group with you."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out loudly and said: "
O people of the trench, Jābir has prepared a feast for you, so come quickly!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said: "
Do not take your pot off the fire and do not bake your dough until I come."
So I came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, leading the people, until I reached my wife, and she said, "This is on you, and on you!"
I said, "I have done just what you told me."
Then I brought out our dough for him, and he spat in it and blessed it. Then he went to our pot, spat in it, and blessed it. Then he said: "
Call a woman baker to bake with you, and ladle out from your pot, but do not take it off the fire."
They were a thousand. I swear by Allah, they ate until they left it and turned away, and our pot was still bubbling as it was, and our dough—or as aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk said—was still being baked as it was.
error: Segment 9: Jābir (the narrator) brought out the dough (فَأَخْرَجْتُ), not his wife; the translation wrongly makes her the subject.

segments_en: The two sons of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam both said: Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from his father,
from Kathīr ibn Farqad, from Nāfiʿ,
that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar
used to walk briskly in his circuits when he arrived for Hajj or ʿUmrah, for three [rounds], and walk normally for four. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that.
error: ابنا means 'the two sons of' ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam, not ʿAbd Allāh himself. The English wrongly made ʿAbd Allāh the narrator and added 'informed us'.

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
all from Ibn
ʿUyaynah—Zuhayr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us—
from Ayyūb ibn Mūsā,
from Nubayh ibn Wahb,
from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUthmān,
who traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"A man in a state of iḥrām may not marry, nor propose."
error: Added clause: 'nor arrange a marriage' has no basis in the Arabic, which has only 'does not marry and does not propose'.

segments_en: Allah wrote a book two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and sent down two verses from it with which He concluded Sūrat al-Baqarah. If they are recited in a house for three nights, Satan will not come near it."
error: The final clause reverses the sense. The Arabic means that when the two verses are recited in a house for three nights, Satan does not come near it. The English says Satan does come near.

segments_en: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man came to him from Yemen and began informing him and telling him, while ʿAlī was there. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, three men came to ʿAlī disputing over a child, [all of whom] had relations with a woman in one period of purity." And he related the rest of the hadith.
error: 'وَعَلِيٌّ بِهَا' means ʿAlī was in Yemen at the time. The translation wrongly says the man was telling the Prophet 'about ʿAlī'.

segments_en: He used to say: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ disliked ten things: yellow [dye], meaning khalūq perfume; changing grey hair; dragging the lower garment; wearing gold rings; displaying adornment in the wrong place; playing with dice; using spells except with the two protective surahs; tying amulets; withdrawing [during intercourse] in an improper manner or place; and harming a child [by intercourse with a nursing mother], without considering it forbidden.
error: The last item is mistranslated. 'فساد الصبي غير محرمه' refers to harming a nursing child by intercourse with its nursing mother, not 'not [that of] his unlawful partner'.

segments_en: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ

sent him to ʿAlī to ask his permission to enter upon Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays, and [ʿAlī] gave him permission. When he had finished his business, the freed slave asked ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ about it, and he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to enter upon women without the permission of their husbands."
error: Reversed subject: ʿAmr sent the freed slave (narrator) to ʿAlī; the English says ʿAmr was sent by him.

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bathed after sexual impurity, Sulaymān said: he would begin by pouring from his right hand onto his left.
And Musaddad said: he washed his hands, pouring the vessel over his right hand. Then they agreed: then he would wash his private parts.

Musaddad said: He would pour onto his left hand, and at times she would allude to the private parts figuratively. Then he would perform his ablution as for prayer, then put his hands into the vessel and run them through his hair, until, when he saw that he had reached the skin, or had cleansed the skin, he would pour water over his head three times. Then, if some water remained, he would pour it over himself.
error: Mistranslation of 'kanat ʿan al-farj': it means she (the narrator) used a euphemism/alluded to the private parts, not 'I was away from the private parts'.

segments_en: We used to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to hear and obey, and then he would say, "As much as you are able." And ʿAlī said, "As much as you [all] are able."
error: The narrator's name 'ʿAlī' (وَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ) is rendered as 'he', so the wording variant is wrongly attributed to the Prophet ﷺ instead of to the narrator ʿAlī.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stood at the well of Badr and said:
"Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?" He said: "They are hearing now what I say to them."
That was mentioned to ʿĀʾishah, and she said, "Ibn ʿUmar was mistaken. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said:
'They now know that what I used to tell them is the truth.'"
Then she recited His words: {Indeed, you do not make the dead hear}, until she had recited the verse.
error: وَهَلَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ means 'Ibn ʿUmar was mistaken/erred'. The translation turned it into a question, 'Did Ibn ʿUmar [really say that]?', which loses ʿĀʾishah's judgment that he made an error.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be in a state of sexual impurity, then sleep as he was, without touching water.
Sufyān said: One day I mentioned the hadith, and Ismāʿīl said to me, "Young man, is this hadith supported by anything?"
error: Ismāʿīl's remark is a question doubting the hadith's support; the translation turns it into a statement affirming that the hadith is strengthened.

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray the forenoon prayer?" She said: "No, except when he came back from an absence."

I asked: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have a particular month that he fasted, other than Ramadan?" She said: "By Allah, he never fasted a particular whole month other than Ramadan until he passed away, and he never left a month without fasting some of it."
error: Second segment: 'wa lā afṭara ḥattā yaṣūma minhu' means he never went without fasting in a month until he had fasted some of it; the translation 'never stopped fasting until he had fasted some of it' garbles this. 'Fasted a particular month' should also be a whole month.

segments_en: From one whom I trust, that Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī

informed him that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made that a concession for the people at the beginning of Islam because of the scarcity of clothing; then he commanded washing and forbade that.
error: مَنْ أَرْضَى (one with whom I am satisfied/whom I trust) was mistranslated as 'From my land', which changes the narrator reference.

segments_en: When the emigrants of the sea returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said:
"Will you not tell me about the most amazing things you saw in the land of Abyssinia?"

Some young men among them said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah. While we were sitting, an old woman from among their elderly nuns passed by us carrying a jug of water on her head. She passed by a young man of theirs, who put one hand between her shoulders and then pushed her, so she fell on her knees and her jug broke. When she got up, she turned to him and said: 'You will come to know, O traitor, when Allah sets up the Throne, gathers the first and the last, and the hands and feet speak of what they used to earn, you will come to know how it stands between you and me with Him tomorrow.'"
He said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"She spoke the truth, she spoke the truth. How can Allah sanctify a people from whose strong the right of their weak is not taken?"
error: Segment 1 wrongly makes the narrator the one who returned ("When I returned"). The Arabic says the emigrants of the sea returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you see those who revile my Companions, say: 'May Allah's curse be upon your evil.'"
error: شَرِّكُمْ means 'your evil'. 'The worse of you' wrongly makes the curse fall on a subset of people instead of on their evil.

segments_en: Regarding the saying of Allah {And to those with whom your oaths have made a pledge, give them their share}, he said: When the Emigrants came to Madinah, the Emigrant would inherit from the Anṣārī instead of the latter's own blood relatives, because of the brotherhood the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had established between them. When this verse was revealed, {And for each We have made heirs of what [parents and relatives] leave}, he said: It abrogated it, {And to those with whom your oaths have made a pledge, give them their share}, meaning support, sincere advice, and aid; and a bequest may be made for him, while inheritance has gone.
error: Reversed the heirs. The Emigrants inherited from the Anṣār instead of the Anṣār's blood relatives, not the other way round.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ swore an oath of abstention from his wives, and he declared [something] forbidden; so he made the forbidden lawful and made expiation for the oath.
error: The verb آلَى (took an oath of abstention, īlāʾ) is mistranslated as a fragment "...to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from his wives". The Prophet ﷺ is the one who swore the oath, but the English leaves out that he did so.

segments_en: The two sons of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording.
error: ابنَي عبد الله بن عمر means 'the two sons of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar'. The translation wrongly makes ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar the speaker's own son ('My two sons, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar'), which misstates the chain of narrators.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said:

"Whoever has a need from Allah or from any of His creation, let him perform ablution, pray two units, and then say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the things that make Your mercy certain, and the resolute means of Your forgiveness, and a share of every good deed, and safety from every sin. I ask You not to leave any sin of mine except that You forgive it, nor any distress except that You relieve it, nor any need with which You are pleased except that You fulfil it for me.' Then let him ask Allah for whatever he wishes of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, for it will be decreed."
error: The passive 'yuqaddaru' (it will be decreed) was mistranslated as 'He is able to do it'.

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ came down from the pulpit on Friday, he would be spoken to about a need.
error: The verb 'yukallamu' is passive: the Prophet was spoken to about a need. The translation reverses this and makes him the speaker.

segments_en: From the Banū Sawāʾah ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿĀʾishah,

regarding the fluid that flows between a man and a woman, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would take a handful of water and pour the water over me, then take another handful of water and pour it over it.
error: The first pouring is mistranslated. Arabic 'yaṣubbu ʿalayya al-māʾ' means he poured the water over me (ʿĀʾishah), not over the fluid.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over a grave after [the deceased] had been buried, and he said the takbīr over it four times.
Al-Shaybānī said: I asked al-Shaʿbī: Who narrated this to you? He said: The trustworthy one, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās.

This is the wording of the hadith of Ḥasan. In the narration of Ibn Numayr he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to a fresh grave and prayed over it, and they lined up behind him, and he said the takbīr four times.
I asked ʿĀmir: Who narrated to you? He said: The trustworthy one who witnessed it, Ibn ʿAbbās.
error: Ḥasan is the narrator's name (the wording of Ḥasan's hadith), not a ḥasan grading of the hadith.

segments_en: Shall I not narrate to you about myself and about the Prophet ﷺ? We said: Yes. She said:
When it was my night, the night he was with me, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, he turned over and placed his sandals by his feet,
and spread the edge of his lower garment over his bed,
and he stayed only as long as he thought I had fallen asleep,
then he put on his sandals gently and took his cloak gently,
then he opened the door gently and went out gently. I put my shift over my head, wrapped myself in my headscarf, and drew my lower garment over me,
and I set out after him until he came to al-Baqīʿ,
where he raised his hands three times, at length,
then he turned away and I turned away; he hurried and I hurried; he ran and I ran;
he went faster and I went faster, and I reached there before him and entered.
I had only just lain down when he came in and said: "
What is the matter, ʿĀʾishah? Why are you out of breath?" She said: Nothing. He said: "
Either you tell me, or the Subtle, the All-Aware will inform me." I said:
O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom! And I told him the matter. He said: "
So you were the dark figure I saw ahead of me?" She said: Yes.
He struck me on the chest with a blow that pained me, then said: "
Did you think that Allah and His Messenger would wrong you?" I said:
However much people conceal, Allah knows it. He said: "
Gabriel came to me when you saw [me], but he did not enter while you had your clothes off. He called me,
and he concealed it from you, so I answered him and concealed it from you,
and I thought you had fallen asleep, and I disliked waking you,
and I feared that you would be frightened to be alone,
and he commanded me to go to al-Baqīʿ and seek forgiveness for them." I said:
How should I say it, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "
Say: Peace be upon the people of these abodes, among the believers and the Muslims,
may Allah have mercy on those of us who have gone before and those who come later,
and we will, Allah willing, join you."
error: Segment 20: it was Gabriel who concealed his call from ʿĀʾishah; the translation makes the Prophet ﷺ the one who concealed it before he answered.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on the pulpit and we sat around him, and he said:
"Among the things I fear for you after me is what will be opened up to you of the blossom of this world and its adornment."

A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, can good bring about evil?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent. It was said to the man, "What is the matter with you? You speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he does not speak to you." We saw that revelation was coming down upon him. Then he recovered, wiping the sweat from himself, and said:

"Indeed, this questioner" and it was as if he approved of him. Then he said: "Good does not bring about evil. Indeed, among what the spring rain makes grow is what kills or nearly kills, except for the animal that eats the green plants: it eats until, when its flanks are full, it faces the sun, passes dung and urine, then goes back to graze. This wealth is green and sweet, and an excellent companion is it for the Muslim, if he gives from it to the poor, the orphan, and the wayfarer" or as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "but whoever takes it without its right is like one who eats and is never satisfied, and it will be a witness against him on the Day of Resurrection."
error: Segment 4 adds an invented question, "Where is the questioner?", which is not in the Arabic. The Arabic begins "Indeed, this questioner..." as a remark praising him.

segments_en: When the news of the Prophet's ﷺ mission in Mecca reached Abū Dharr, he said to his brother, "Ride to this valley and find out for me about this man who claims that news comes to him from the heaven. Listen to what he says, then come back to me."

So the other man set out until he reached Mecca, and he listened to what he said. Then he returned to Abū Dharr and said, "I saw him commanding noble character, and [speaking] words that are not poetry."
Abū Dharr said, "You have not satisfied me in what I wanted."

So he prepared provisions and carried a water skin of his containing water until he reached Mecca. He came to the mosque and looked for the Prophet ﷺ, but he did not know him, and he disliked asking about him. Then night overtook him and he lay down. ʿAlī saw him and realized that he was a stranger. When Abū Dharr saw him, he followed him, and neither of them asked the other about anything until morning. Then he took up his water skin and provisions to the mosque and spent that day without seeing the Prophet ﷺ, until evening came and he returned to his place of lying down. ʿAlī passed by him and said, "Is it not yet time for the man to know his lodging?" So he made him get up and took him along with him, and neither of them asked the other about anything. When the third day came, he did the same, and ʿAlī made him get up with him. Then he said to him, "Will you not tell me what brought you to this town?" He said, "If you give me a covenant and a pledge that you will guide me, I will do so."

Abū Dharr did so, and told him. ʿAlī said, "It is true, and he is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When morning comes, follow me. If I see anything I fear for you, I will stop as though I am pouring out water. If I keep going, follow me until you enter where I enter."
He did so and went following him until he entered upon the Prophet ﷺ, and he entered with him. He listened to his words and accepted Islam on the spot. The Prophet ﷺ said to him,
"Return to your people and inform them, until my instruction comes to you."
He said, "By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will proclaim it loudly among them."
He went out until he came to the mosque and called out at the top of his voice, "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

The people rose up and beat him until they laid him down. Then al-ʿAbbās came and threw himself over him and said, "Woe to you! Do you not know that he is from Ghifār, and that the route of your caravans to Syria passes by them?"
So he rescued him from them. Then the next day he returned and did the same, and they rose up against him and beat him, and al-ʿAbbās threw himself over him and rescued him.
error: Segment 5: the one who gave the covenant and told ʿAlī his purpose was Abū Dharr, not ʿAlī.

segments_en: Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah sent him with milk, colostrum, and small cucumbers to the Prophet ﷺ, while the Prophet ﷺ was at the upper part of the valley. He said: I entered upon him without giving greetings of peace and without asking permission, so the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Go back and say: 'Peace be upon you, may I enter?'"
That was after Ṣafwān had become Muslim.
error: لِبَإٍ (colostrum, the first milk) was mistranslated as "young gazelle meat", which changes what was sent.

segments_en: Some slaves went out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, meaning on the day of Ḥudaybiyah, before the treaty. Their masters wrote to him, saying: "O Muḥammad, by Allah, they did not come out to you out of desire for your religion; they only came out to flee from slavery." Some people said: "They speak the truth, O Messenger of Allah; return them to them."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry and said:
"I do not see you ceasing, O assembly of Quraysh, until Allah sends against you someone who will strike your necks over this."
And he refused to return them, and said:
"They are those freed by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
error: عبدان is a plural (some slaves); the translation wrongly limits it to 'Two slaves', inventing a number.

segments_en: When the waiting period of Zaynab ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd: "Mention her to me."
Zayd said: So I went and said: O Zaynab, glad tidings! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has sent me to you, mentioning you [for marriage].
She said: I will not do anything until I consult my Lord. So she stood at her place of prayer, and the Qurʾān was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered without permission.
error: Reversed object: the Prophet told Zayd to mention Zaynab to him (اذكرها علي), not to mention himself to her.

segments_en: People used to be commanded that a man place his right hand on his left forearm in prayer.
Abū Ḥāzim said: I only know that he attributed that to the Prophet ﷺ.
Ismāʿīl said: It is attributed.
And he did not say "he attributes".
error: Segment 3: يُنْمَى is passive ("It is attributed"), not active "He attributes". The translation as written contradicts the next segment, which says he did not say "he attributes".

segments_en: I set out,
and there was a shepherd driving his sheep. I said: "To whom do you belong?" He said: "To a man of Quraysh," and he named him, and I knew him.
I said: "Is there any milk in your flock?" He said: "Yes."
I said: "Will you milk for me?" He said: "Yes."
So I told him, and he tied up one sheep from his flock.
Then I told him to wipe the dust from its udder,
then I told him to wipe his hands.
He said: "Like this," striking one palm against the other. Then he milked a small amount of milk. I had prepared for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a leather container with a piece of cloth over its mouth,
and I poured [water] over the milk,
until its bottom became cool,
then I reached the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Drink, O Messenger of Allah."
He drank until I was satisfied.
error: Segment 9 reverses the action: the Arabic says water was poured over the milk (صببت على اللبن), not the milk poured over the container.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while I was screened with a curtain that had a picture on it. His face changed colour, then he took hold of the curtain and tore it down. Then he said:
"Among the people who will be most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who imitate the creation of Allah."
error: The translation adds "[a shelf]", which is not in the Arabic. She says she was screening herself (مُتَسَتِّرَةٌ) with the curtain, not that she covered a shelf.

segments_en: Indeed, your Lord is Modest (Ḥayiyy) and Generous. He is shy before His servant when he raises his hands to Him, to return them empty"—or he said, "disappointed."
error: حَيِيٌّ means Modest/Shy, not 'Ever-Living'. The translation misstates the attribute, and it also contradicts the following clause about Allah being shy.

segments_en: ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad asked permission to enter upon ʿAbdullāh, and we had been sitting at his door for a long time. The slave girl came out and asked permission for them, and he permitted them. Then he stood and prayed, standing between me and [the other]. Then he said: "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do."
