error: Position reversed: the Arabic says ʿAbdullāh prayed between the narrator and the other man, not that the narrator stood between ʿAbdullāh and them.

segments_en: Ubayy said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a hare he had roasted, and bread. He placed it before the Prophet ﷺ and then said, "I found that it bleeds."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions:
"It does no harm; eat." And he said to the Bedouin, "Eat."
He said, "I am fasting." He said, "What fast?"
He said, "Fasting three days of the month." He said:
"If you are fasting, then keep to the bright white days: the thirteenth, the fourteenth and the fifteenth."
error: The narrator is named Ubayy (أُبَيّ) in the Arabic. The translation renders it as "My father", which misattributes the report.

segments_en: and Ḥamzah,
the two sons of ʿAbdullāh, from their father,
from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transfer of chain.) And Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā and ʿAmr al-Nāqid narrated to us,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb, from Sufyān, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father,
from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transfer of chain.) And ʿAmr al-Nāqid narrated to us,
Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ,
from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim and Ḥamzah,
the two sons of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transfer of chain.) And ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather,
ʿUqayl ibn Khālid narrated to me,
(Transfer of chain.) And Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā narrated it to us,
Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal informed us,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn
Isḥāq. (Transfer of chain.) And ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Dārimī narrated to me,
Abū al-Yamān informed us: Shuʿayb informed us,
all of them from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father,
from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning ill omen.
Like the hadith of Mālik. None of them mentions, in the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, 'contagion' and 'bird omens', except Yūnus ibn Yazīd.
error: Segment 18: الْعَدْوَى means 'contagion', not 'the ʿAdawī' (a tribal/person nisba).

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not grant ruqbā and do not grant ʿumrā; whoever is granted something as ruqbā or ʿumrā, it belongs to his heirs."
error: The verbs are passive (أُرْقِبَ/أُعْمِرَ): it is the recipient whose heirs inherit. The translation makes the one who grants the gift the subject, which reverses who inherits.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ set out from Madinah in Ramadan,
with ten thousand men,
and that was at the end of eight and a half years after his arrival in Madinah.
He and the Muslims with him travelled to Makkah,
he fasting and they fasting, until he reached al-Kadīd, a watering place between ʿUsfān and Qudayd, [where] he broke his fast and they broke their fast.
Az-Zuhrī said: Only the latest, and then the latest, of the commands of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is to be taken.
error: Segment 3 mistranslates 'eight and a half years' as 'the beginning of the eighth year and a half', which changes the date. Segment 6 misrenders 'al-ākhir fal-ākhir' (the latest, then the latest) as 'the latest... then the one after it'.

segments_en: He used to breathe three times while drinking from the vessel, and Anas claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to breathe three times while drinking from the vessel.
error: Wrong subject: the Arabic says Anas himself claimed this (وَزَعَمَ أَنَسٌ). The translation has an unnamed 'he' claiming that Anas said it.

segments_en: And my eyes saw,
when the Prophet ﷺ spoke, and he said:
"Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor,
and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest with his due gift."
He said: What is his due gift, O Messenger of Allah? He said:
"A day and a night, and hospitality is three days,
and whatever is beyond that is charity for him,
and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent."
error: Added clause: 'and my ears heard' is not in the Arabic of segment 2, which only says the eyes saw.

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said] to the two of them when they read the letter of Musaylimah:
"What do the two of you say?"
They said, "We say as he said." He said:
"By Allah, were it not that envoys are not killed, I would have struck off your necks."
error: The Arabic قَرَآ is dual: the two men read Musaylimah's letter. The English says 'he read', which gives the wrong subject.

segments_en: We besieged the fortress of aṭ-Ṭāʾif with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Muʿādh said: I heard my father say "the castle of aṭ-Ṭāʾif" and "the stronghold of aṭ-Ṭāʾif," all of these. Then I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Whoever delivers an arrow in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will have a rank [in Paradise]."
And he went on with the hadith. And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"Any Muslim man who frees a Muslim man, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will make every bone of the freed man a protection from the Fire for the corresponding bone of the one who freed him. And any woman who frees a Muslim woman, Allah will make every bone of the freed woman a protection from the Fire for the corresponding bone of the one who freed her, on the Day of Resurrection."
error: In the woman's case the roles are reversed. The Arabic makes the bones of the freed woman the protection for the bones of the freer; the translation has the freer's bones protecting the freer.

segments_en: A funeral passed by the two of them; one stood and the other sat. The one who stood said, "By Allah, I know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood." The one who sat said to him, "I know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [also] sat."
error: The Arabic "ʿalimtu" is first person ("I know"), but the translation renders it as "you know", which changes who is asserting the knowledge.

segments_en: I cut a boy's ear—or my ear was cut. Then Abū Bakr came to us on Hajj, and we gathered to him, and we brought the matter before ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. ʿUmar said: This [boy] has reached the age for retaliation. Call a cupper for me so that retaliation may be taken from him. When the cupper was called, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"I gave my maternal aunt a boy as a gift, hoping that she would be blessed in him. I said to her: Do not hand him over to a cupper, nor a goldsmith, nor a butcher."
error: Wrong subject: the Arabic says "I cut" (قَطَعْتُ) a boy's ear, but the translation says a boy's ear was cut, dropping the speaker as the one who did it.

segments_en: That Fāṭimah

wept over the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he died, and she said, "O my father, how near he is to his Lord! O my father, to Jibrīl we announce his death! O my father, whose abode is the Paradise of Firdaws!"
error: The Arabic "مِنْ رَبِّهِ مَا أَدْنَاهُ" means "how near he is to his Lord". The translation adds "who answered the call of his Lord", which is not in the text, and makes "to him" ambiguous.

segments_en: There was a man from the Anṣār who, whenever he was absent from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I was present, I would come to him with what had happened with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and whenever I was absent from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he was present, he would come to me with what had happened with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
error: The first clause reverses the roles. The Arabic says the narrator would come to the Anṣārī man (أتيته) when the man was absent. The translation has the man coming to the narrator.

segments_en: I came to Syria and prayed two rakʿahs,
then I said, "O Allah, make easy for me a righteous companion."
So I came to some people and sat with them,
and an elderly man came and sat beside me.
I asked, "Who is this?" They said, "Abū al-Dardāʾ."
I said to him, "I asked Allah to make easy for me a righteous companion, and He has made you [one] for me."
He asked, "Where are you from?" I said, "From the people of Kufa."

He said, "Do you not have with you the son of Umm ʿAbd, the keeper of the sandals, the cushion, and the purification vessel? And among you is the one whom Allah protected from Satan upon the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ. And do you not have among you the keeper of the secret of the Prophet ﷺ, which no one else knows?" Then he said, "How does ʿAbdullāh recite {By the night when it covers}?"
So I recited to him: {By the night when it covers, and the day when it appears, and the male and the female.}
He said, "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught it to me directly from his mouth to mine."
error: Segment 9 adds "He who created" to the recitation; the Arabic reads simply "and the male and the female". This changes the wording of the recited verse, which is the point of the report.

segments_en: When one of us was menstruating,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to have contact with her,
he would order her to wrap an izār around herself at the height of her menstruation, and then he would have contact with her.
She said, "And which of you can control his desire as the Prophet ﷺ controlled his desire?"
error: The Arabic says 'his desire' (إربه), not 'her desire'; the translation wrongly makes the one controlling desire female.

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which deed is best?" He said:
"Prayer at its proper time."
I said, "Then which?" He said:
"Then dutifulness to parents."
I said, "Then which?" He said:
"Striving in the cause of Allah."
Then I fell silent with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and had I asked for more, he would have given me more.
error: Wrong subject: it is Ibn Masʿūd who fell silent (stopped asking), not the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for prayer, and those with him stood. He stood for a long time. Then he bowed and made the bowing long. Then he raised his head and prostrated and made the prostration long. Then he raised his head and sat and made the sitting long. Then he prostrated and made the prostration long. Then he raised his head and stood, and in the second rakʿah he did the same as he had done in the first rakʿah of standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting. At the end of his prostration in the second rakʿah he began to blow, and he wept and said:
"Did You not promise me this while I am among them? Did You not promise me this while we are seeking Your forgiveness?"
Then he raised his head, and the sun cleared. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and addressed the people. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said:

"The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So when you see an eclipse of either of them, hasten to the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, Paradise was brought near to me until, had I stretched out my hand, I could have taken some of its clusters. And the Fire was brought near to me until I began to shield myself from it, fearing that it would envelop you. I even saw in it a woman of Ḥimyar being punished on account of a cat that she had tied up; she neither let it eat from the creatures of the earth, nor did she feed it or give it water, until it died. I saw it clawing at her when she came forward, and when she turned away it clawed at her rear. I also saw in it the man with the two sibtī sandals, the brother of Banū ad-Daʿdāʿ, being pushed into the Fire with a two-pronged staff. And I saw in it the owner of the curved staff, who used to steal from the pilgrims with his curved staff, leaning on his staff in the Fire and saying: 'I am the thief of the curved staff.'"
error: Wrong voice/subject: the man of the two sibtiyyah is being pushed (yudfaʿu, passive) with a two-pronged staff, not pushing himself along. Also sibtiyyatayn are sandals/shoes, not cloaks.

segments_en: Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth said to him: "What prevents you from speaking to your maternal uncle ʿUthmān about his brother al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah? People have said a great deal about what he has done."
ʿUbaydullāh said: So I stood waiting for ʿUthmān when he came out to the prayer, and I said to him, "I have a need to put to you, and it is a piece of advice."
He said, "O man,
I seek refuge in Allah from you," so I left.
When the prayer was finished, I sat with al-Miswar and Ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth,
and I told them what I had said to ʿUthmān and what he had said to me.
They said, "You have done what was incumbent upon you."
While I was sitting with them,
the messenger of ʿUthmān came to me,
and they said to me, "Allah has put you to the test."
So I went until I entered upon him,
and he said, "What is this advice of yours that you mentioned a moment ago?" I said the testimony of faith and then said, "Allah sent Muḥammad ﷺ and revealed the Book to him,
and you were among those who responded to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ and believed in him,
and you made the two earlier migrations,
and you accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and saw his guidance,
and people have spoken much about the matter of al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah,
so it is your duty to carry out the legal punishment on him."
He said to me, "O son of my brother, did you meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" I said, "No,
but knowledge of him has reached me as it reaches a maiden in her seclusion."
He said: Then ʿUthmān recited the testimony of faith and said, "Allah sent Muḥammad ﷺ with the truth and revealed the Book to him,
and I was among those who responded to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ and believed in what Muḥammad ﷺ was sent with.
And I made the two earlier migrations, as you said,
and I accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him.
By Allah, I never disobeyed him nor deceived him until Allah took him in death.
Then Allah appointed Abū Bakr as successor, and by Allah, I never disobeyed him nor deceived him.
Then ʿUmar was appointed successor,
and by Allah, I never disobeyed him nor deceived him. Then I was made successor.
Do I not have the same right over you that they had over me?" I said, "Yes."
He said, "Then what are these reports that reach me from you? As for what you mentioned about al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah,
we shall deal with it, Allah willing, in accordance with the truth." He said: So al-Walīd was flogged forty lashes,
and [ʿUthmān] ordered ʿAlī to flog him,
and [ʿAlī] was the one who flogged him.
Yūnus and the son of the brother of al-Zuhrī said, from al-Zuhrī: "Do I not have the same right over you as they had?"
error: Segments 13-15: ʿUbaydullāh is addressing ʿUthmān, so the Arabic has 'you were / you made the migrations / you accompanied'; the English wrongly uses 'I', changing the subject.

segments_en: She is trustworthy, a woman of truthfulness. She said: While my father was on a military expedition in the Jāhiliyyah, they were scorched by the heat of the ground, and a man said: Who will give me his sandals, and I will marry to him the first daughter born to me? So my father took off his sandals and threw them to him. Then a daughter was born to him and she reached maturity. And he mentioned something similar, but did not mention the story of the grey hair.
error: مُصَدَّقَةٌ means 'trusted/credible' (a statement about the woman's reliability), not 'one who was given a dowry'.

segments_en: He was at the funeral of ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ, and we were walking at a light (fairly quick) pace. Abū Bakrah caught up with us, raised his whip, and said: "I have seen us with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we used to walk at a brisk pace."
error: خفيفًا (light/fairly quick) was mistranslated as 'slow', which reverses the sense: Abū Bakrah is rebuking them for not walking briskly enough.

segments_en: Zaynab, the wife of ʿAbdullāh, from Zaynab,

said: An old woman used to visit us and perform ruqyah for erysipelas. We had a bed with long legs, and whenever ʿAbdullāh came in, he would clear his throat and make a noise. One day he entered, and when she heard his voice she veiled herself from him. He came and sat beside me and touched me, and he felt a thread. He said: What is this? I said: A ruqyah was performed for me with it for erysipelas. He pulled it and cut it, and threw it away, and said: The family of ʿAbdullāh have no need of polytheism. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Spells, amulets, and love charms are polytheism."
I said: One day I went out and so-and-so saw me, and my eye on his side began to water. When I perform ruqyah on it, its tears subside, and when I leave it, it waters.

He said: That is Satan. If you obey him, he leaves you, and if you disobey him, he pokes your eye with his finger. But if you did as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did, it would be better for you and more fitting for your cure: sprinkle water in your eye and say: "
Remove the affliction, O Lord of the people, heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing except Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness behind."
error: Wrong subject in segment 2: it was the old woman who veiled herself from ʿAbdullāh when she heard his voice, not the narrator (Zaynab).

segments_en: I was with ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, when an Iraqi man came to her and said, "Which shroud is best?" She said, "Woe to you! What harm does it do you?" He said, "Mother of the Believers, show me your copy of the Qurʾān."
She said, "Why?" He said, "So that I may arrange the Qurʾān according to it, for it is being recited without arrangement."
She said, "What harm does it do you which part you recite first?
The first thing to be revealed of it was a sura from the mufaṣṣal, in which Paradise and the Fire are mentioned, until, when people had turned to Islam, the lawful and the unlawful were revealed.
Had the first thing revealed been, 'Do not drink wine,'
they would have said, 'We will never give up wine.' And had it been, 'Do not commit adultery,'
they would have said, 'We will never give up adultery.'

Indeed, there was revealed in Makkah to Muhammad ﷺ, while I was a young girl playing, {Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more grievous and more bitter}. And Sūrat al-Baqarah and Sūrat an-Nisāʾ were not revealed except while I was with him."
He said: So she brought out the copy of the Qurʾān for him, and she dictated to him the verses of the suras.
error: Segment 9: آيَ السُّوَرِ means the verses of the suras, not the order of the suras.

segments_en: The Quraysh
made a treaty with the Prophet ﷺ, and among their representatives was Suhayl ibn ʿAmr. The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAlī: "
Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."
Suhayl said: "As for 'In the name of Allah,' we do not know what 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful' is. Rather, write what we know: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" So he said: "
Write: From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah."
They said: "If we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would follow you. Rather, write your name and the name of your father." So the Prophet ﷺ said: "
Write: From Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullāh."

They stipulated to the Prophet ﷺ that whoever of you comes to us, we will not return him to you, and whoever of us comes to you, you will return him to us. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we write this?" He said: "
Yes. Whoever of us goes to them, Allah has put him far away; and whoever of them comes to us, Allah will make for him relief and a way out."
error: Segment 8 reverses the stipulation. Quraysh said they would not return anyone who came to them from the Muslims, and the Muslims must return anyone who came to the Muslims from Quraysh. The translation has the directions and parties confused.

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he came upon a woman close to giving birth at the door of a tent, and he said:
"Perhaps he intends to have relations with her?" They said: Yes.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I had intended to curse him with a curse that would accompany him into his grave. How could he make him his heir when he is not lawful for him? How could he take him as a servant when he is not lawful for him?"
error: أَتَى is active: the Prophet came upon the woman. The translation makes it passive (a woman was brought to him), which changes who did what.

segments_en: There was a man among the Anṣār called Abū Shuʿayb,
and he had a slave who was a butcher. He said, "Prepare a meal for me, for I want to invite the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as the fifth of five."
So he invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as the fifth of five,
and a man followed them. The Prophet ﷺ said,
"You invited us as the fifth of five, and this man has followed us.
If you wish, you may permit him [to enter],
and if you wish, you may leave him."
He said, "Rather, I permit him."

Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl say: When people are at a dining spread, they should not pass food from one spread to another; rather, they may pass it to one another at that same spread, or leave it.
error: Segment 7: the Prophet tells Abū Shuʿayb he may leave the man (you may leave him); the translation wrongly makes the Prophet the one who will leave him.

segments_en: He asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which charity is best. He said:
"The service of a servant in the cause of Allah, or the shade of a tent, or a she-camel ready for breeding [given] in the cause of Allah."
error: طَرُوقَةُ فَحْلٍ is a she-camel old enough to be covered by the stud, not a 'mature male camel'; this changes the gender of the animal given.

segments_en: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was taken up into Paradise, or as he said, a river appeared before him, its two banks of hollowed rubies (or he said, hollow-cored rubies),
and the angel who was with him struck his hand and brought out musk. Muḥammad ﷺ said to the angel who was with him: "What is this?" He said:
This is al-Kawthar, which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has given you.
error: الْيَاقُوتُ (rubies) was mistranslated as 'pearl-like jewels', which changes the material of the riverbanks.

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said, "O Messenger of Allah, will the people return with two rewards while I return with one?" So he commanded ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr to take her to al-Tanʿīm.
She said: So he seated me behind him on a camel of his. She said: I began to lift my head covering and uncover it from my neck, and he would strike my foot under the pretext of [striking] the mount.
I said to him, "Do you see anyone?" She said: Then I entered the state of iḥrām for ʿUmrah, and we came back until we reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was at al-Ḥaṣbah.
error: بِعِلَّةِ الرَّاحِلَةِ means 'under the pretext of (striking) the mount'. The translation 'with the sandal-strap of the mount' is a mistranslation that changes the fact described.

segments_en: He went out on Hajj, and when he was at al-Suwaydāʾ, there was a man who had come as if seeking medicine and aloe. He said, "One who heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the Farewell Hajj told me, as he was admonishing the people, commanding them and forbidding them, that he said:
'O people, take the stipend as long as it is a stipend. But when the Quraysh contend with one another over kingship, and it comes at the expense of the religion of any of you, then leave it.'"
error: The Arabic is a report, "one who heard the Messenger told me". The English turns it into a command addressed to the listener, "Tell me, [you] who heard".

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to enter the house of Umm Sulaym and sleep on her bed while she was not there. One day he came and slept on her bed. She was approached and told, "The Prophet ﷺ is sleeping in your house, on your bed." She came, and he had sweated, and his sweat had collected on a piece of leather on the bed. She opened her container and began to wipe up that sweat and wring it into her bottles. The Prophet ﷺ was startled and said,
"What are you doing, Umm Sulaym?"
She said, "O Messenger of Allah, we hope for its blessing for our children." He said, "You have done right."
error: Wrong subject: the Arabic says Umm Sulaym was approached and told (fa-utiyat), not 'I came'.

segments_en: He added this: Then the Prophet ﷺ said to the one who bit,
"If you wish, you may let him have your hand so that he bites it, and then you pull it out of his mouth."
And he voided the blood-money for his teeth.
error: Reversed roles in the biting scenario: the Arabic says the biter (the other party) bites the hand and it is pulled from his mouth, not that the biter's hand is put in the other's mouth.

segments_en: Cities will be opened up for you,

and there will be mobilized armies, and expeditions will be assigned to you among them. A man among you will dislike being sent on an expedition, so he will free himself from his people, then go around the tribes offering himself to them, saying:
'Whom can I spare the expedition of such-and-such?
Whom can I spare the expedition of such-and-such?' Such a man is a hired hand, down to the last drop of his blood."
error: Reversed roles: the man offers to go in place of others (relieving them of the expedition), not asking someone to take his place.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Sūrat Tabārak on Friday while standing.
He reminded us of the Days of Allah, while Abū al-Dardāʾ or Abū Dharr was nudging me. He said:
"When was this sūrah revealed?
I had not heard it until now." So he gestured to him to be quiet.
When they finished the prayer, he said:
"I asked you when this sūrah was revealed and you did not tell me?" Ubayy said:
"You have nothing from your prayer today except what you wasted in idle talk."
So he went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, mentioned that to him, and told him what Ubayy had said.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ubayy spoke the truth."
error: Ubayy is rendered as 'my father' in segments 6 and 8; the Arabic names Ubayy, so the speaker is misidentified.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Abraham migrated with Sarah, and they gave her Hagar,
and she returned and said, 'Did you realize that Allah has humbled the disbeliever and given [me] a servant girl?'"
Ibn Sīrīn said, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "And he gave her Hagar as a servant."
error: آجَرَ is the name Hagar (the servant given to Sarah), not 'a reward [or: gift]'.

segments_en: That Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq
wrote for him: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

This is the obligation of charity (ṣadaqah) which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made obligatory upon the Muslims, and which Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to impose. Regarding the ages of camels within the obligations for livestock: whoever owes, from his camels, the charity of a jadhaʿah but does not have a jadhaʿah and has a ḥiqqah, the ḥiqqah is to be accepted from him, and the collector is to give in its place two sheep, if they are easily available, or twenty dirhams. Whoever owes the charity of a ḥiqqah but has only a bint labūn, the bint labūn is to be accepted from him, and he gives along with it two sheep or twenty dirhams. Whoever owes a bint labūn but does not have one and has a ḥiqqah, the ḥiqqah is to be accepted from him, and the collector gives him twenty dirhams or two sheep. Whoever owes a bint labūn but does not have one and has a bint makhāḍ, the bint makhāḍ is to be accepted from him, and he gives along with it twenty dirhams or two sheep.

Whoever owes a bint makhāḍ but does not have one and has a bint labūn, the bint labūn is to be accepted from him, and the collector gives him twenty dirhams or two sheep. And whoever does not have a bint makhāḍ of the proper kind but has a male ibn labūn, it is to be accepted from him, and nothing further is due with it.
error: In the jadhaʿah/ḥiqqah case the owner gives the lower animal, so the collector gives the two sheep or twenty dirhams. The translation says 'he is to add', which wrongly makes the owner the one who pays.

segments_en: I attended the Friday prayer with al-Ḥajjāj, and he gave a sermon, and he mentioned the hadith of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh. He said in it: "So listen and obey the caliph of Allah and His chosen one, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān."
And he related the hadith. He said: "And if I seized Rabīʿah for [the crimes of] Muḍar," and he did not mention the story of al-Ḥamrāʾ.
error: جَمَّعْتُ means he attended the Friday (congregational) prayer, not that he performed Hajj.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was occupied one night and could not pray it,
so he delayed it until we had fallen asleep in the mosque,
then we woke up, then slept, then woke up again,
then the Prophet ﷺ came out to us and said:
"None of the people of the earth is waiting for the prayer except you."
Ibn ʿUmar did not mind whether he prayed it early or delayed it, as long as he did not fear that sleep would overcome him and make him miss its time,
and he would sleep before it.
Ibn Jurayj said: I said to ʿAṭāʾ, and he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer one night until the people had slept and woken up, and slept and woken up,
then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb stood up and said: "The prayer!"
ʿAṭāʾ said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came out, as though I am looking at him now,
with water dripping from his head,
placing his hand on his head, and he said:
"Were it not that I would be placing a hardship on my Ummah, I would have commanded them to pray it like this."
I asked ʿAṭāʾ to confirm how the Prophet ﷺ had placed his hand on his head, as Ibn ʿAbbās had informed him,
so ʿAṭāʾ spread his fingers apart for me somewhat,
then placed the tips of his fingers on the side of the head and then brought them together,
passing them over the head like that until his thumb touched the edge of the ear nearest the face, by the temple and the side of the beard,
neither shortening nor hurrying except like that, and he said:
"Were it not that I would be placing a hardship on my Ummah, I would have commanded them to pray like this."
error: Segment 15: Ibn Jurayj (the narrator) asked ʿAṭāʾ to confirm the manner; the translation wrongly makes ʿAṭāʾ the one who made sure.

segments_en: The two best men, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, nearly perished: they raised their voices in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ when the riders of Banū Tamīm came to him.
One of them pointed to al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, of Banū Mujāshiʿ,
and the other pointed to a different man (Nāfiʿ said: I do not remember his name). Abū Bakr said to ʿUmar: You only wanted to oppose me.
He said: I did not want to oppose you.
Their voices rose over that,
so Allah revealed: {O you who believe, do not raise your voices...} the verse.
Ibn al-Zubayr said: After this verse, ʿUmar would not make the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hear him (he spoke so softly) until the Prophet asked him to clarify what he said.
He did not mention that about his father,
meaning Abū Bakr.
error: Segment 7: the one who asks for clarification is the Prophet (yastafhimuhu), not ʿUmar. The translation reverses this, making ʿUmar ask the Prophet to repeat himself.

segments_en: […] Sahl? I said, "Yes."
He said: I bear witness about Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that I heard him adding to it:
"I will say: 'They are of me.'
It will be said: 'You do not know what they introduced after you.'
I will say: 'Away, away with whoever changed [things] after me!'"
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Suḥqan means "far away."
It is said "saḥīq" means far; and "asḥaqahu" means he removed it far away.
error: Sahl is the person asked about, not the speaker. The Arabic has no "said", so "Sahl said" wrongly attributes the question and answer to Sahl.

segments_en: A group of people from ʿUraynah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, accepted Islam and pledged allegiance to him, and the mūm—which is birsām (pleurisy)—had broken out in Madinah. Then he mentioned it similar to their hadith and added: and with him were young men of the Anṣār, about twenty, so he sent them after them and sent with them a tracker to follow their trail.
error: The Arabic says about twenty young men of the Anṣār. The translation adds 'horsemen', which the text does not say.

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:

"A man visited a brother of his in another town, so Allah stationed an angel on his path. When he came upon him, the angel said: Where do you intend to go? He said: I intend to visit a brother of mine in this town.
The angel said: Do you have some favor over him that you are looking after? He said: No, except that I love him for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
The angel said: I am a messenger to you from Allah, [to tell you] that Allah loves you as you loved him for His sake."
error: Segment 3 reversed the favor: the angel asks whether the man has a favor over his brother that he is tending (لك عليه), not whether he owes his brother a favor.

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting on the pulpit: {And they will call, "O Mālik, let your Lord put an end to us."} Qatādah said: [This is] an example for later generations, an admonition for those who come after them.

Another said: {muqrinīn} means those who are able to control; it is said, "So-and-so is muqrin for so-and-so," meaning he is in control of him. And the akwāb are the pitchers that have no spouts. {The first of the worshippers}, that is: it was not so (there is no son), so I am the first of those who refuse; the two forms are both dialects, ʿābid and ʿabid, and ʿAbd Allāh recited {and the Messenger said, "O my Lord"}. It is also said: {the first of the worshippers} means the first of those who deny, from ʿabada, yaʿbadu.
error: "ما كان" is a negation ("it was not so / there was no son"), but the translation renders it as a conditional "if there were [a son]", which reverses the sense of the gloss.

segments_en: I saw Sharīk lead us in the ʿAṣr prayer at a funeral; he placed his cap in front of him—meaning during an obligatory prayer that had come due.
error: The Arabic says Sharīk led the ʿAṣr prayer while at a funeral. The translation turns it into a funeral prayer held at ʿAṣr time, which changes what prayer was performed.

segments_en: It was reported to ʿUmar that Samurah
had sold wine. He said, "May Allah fight Samurah! Did he not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'May Allah fight the Jews! Fats were forbidden to them, so they melted them down.'"
Sufyān said: "That is, they melted them."
error: The English adds "and sold them" to the Arabic "فجملوها", which only says they melted the fats.

segments_en: With this account, he said: He was invited on the third day and did not respond, and he pelted the messenger with stones.
error: The Arabic verb is active (وحصبَ الرسولَ, 'he pelted the messenger'), with the invited man as subject. The English passive hides who did it.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the ʿaqīqah for al-Ḥasan with a sheep and said:
"O Fāṭimah, shave his head and give in charity the weight of his hair in silver."
He said: So she weighed it, and it weighed one dirham or part of a dirham.
error: Wrong subject in segment 3: فَوَزَنَتْهُ is feminine ('she weighed it', i.e. Fāṭimah), not 'I weighed it'.

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ and he reminded us of Paradise and the Fire.
Then he mentioned [a narration] similar to their hadith.
error: Wrong subject: the Arabic says the Prophet reminded us (فَذَكَّرَنَا), not that we mentioned them.

segments_en: that the two of them
witnessed Abū Burdah narrating to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from his father,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"No Muslim man dies except that Allah will put in his place a Jew or a Christian in the Fire."

He said: So ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz made him swear three times by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, that his father had narrated it to him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he swore to him. [The narrator] said: Saʿīd did not tell me that he had made him swear, but he did not object to ʿAwn's statement.
error: Wrong subject/object: Saʿīd did not object to ʿAwn's statement; the translation says ʿAwn did not object to what 'I' said.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You will come to me with bright faces and bright limbs from ablution. This is the mark of my community; no one else has it."
error: The translation adds "at the Basin", which is not in the Arabic text of this narration.

segments_en: I asked Lāḥiq about the two rakʿahs

before sunset. He said, "ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr used to pray them, so Muʿāwiyah sent to him asking, 'What are these two rakʿahs at sunset?'" The report was referred to Umm Salamah, and Umm Salamah said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray two rakʿahs before ʿAṣr, but he was kept busy from them, so he prayed them when the sun had set. I never saw him pray them before or after."
error: Lāḥiq is a person's name (the one asked), not an adverb; "I later asked" wrongly drops him as the person questioned.

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās had three young slaves who were cuppers. Two of them earned a daily payment for him and his family, and one would perform cupping on him and his family.
He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"What an excellent servant is the cupper: he removes the blood, lightens the back, and clears the sight."
He also said that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken up on the Night Journey, he did not pass by any company of angels except that they said, "Upon you is cupping." And he said:
"The best days on which you can have cupping done are the seventeenth, the nineteenth, and the twenty-first." And he said:
"The best of what you can use for treatment is snuff, medicine poured into the side of the mouth, cupping, and a laxative."
Al-ʿAbbās and his Companions poured medicine into the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Who gave me this medicine?" They all held back, so he said:
"No one in the house will be left without having this medicine poured into his mouth."
except for his uncle al-ʿAbbās. ʿAbd said: Al-Naḍr said: Ladūd is the same as wajūr (medicine poured into the mouth).
error: Subject and object reversed in segment 7: al-ʿAbbās and his companions poured the medicine into the Prophet's mouth, not the other way around.

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey. He said: The provisions of the people ran out, until he was about to slaughter some of their pack animals. He said: Then ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, if you were to gather what remains of the people's provisions and then supplicate to Allah over them..."

He said: So he did so. He said: Then the one with wheat came with his wheat, and the one with dates came with his dates. He said: Mujāhid said: And the one with date stones came with his date stones. I said, "What did they do with the date stones?" He said, "They would suck on them and drink water over them."
He said: Then he supplicated over them, until the people filled their provision bags. He said: Then at that point he said,

"I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. No servant will meet Allah with these two [testimonies], without doubting them, except that he will enter Paradise."
error: Wrong subject: 'هَمَّ' is singular and refers to the Prophet ﷺ, who was about to slaughter some of their pack animals. The translation says 'they were about to slaughter'.

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, which charity (ṣadaqah) is greatest in reward? He said:

"By your father, I will tell you: that you give charity while you are healthy and stingy, fearing poverty and hoping for a long life; and do not delay until, when [the soul] reaches the throat, you say: 'Give so-and-so such and such, and so-and-so such and such,' when it already belongs to so-and-so."
error: تَأْمُلُ الْبَقَاءَ means hoping for a long life (survival), not hoping for wealth.

segments_en: With the meaning of the chain of Abū Tawbah and his report. He said, at the saying:
"what will pay on my behalf."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent toward me, and I was distressed by it.
error: فَاغْتَمَزْتُهَا (in the parallel narration, فَاغْتَمَمْتُهَا) means Bilāl was distressed or aggrieved by the silence, not that he "took it as a hint".

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began the prayer, he would say the takbīr and then say:

"I have turned my face to the One who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining to the truth, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has no partner. This I have been commanded, and I am among the Muslims. O Allah, You are the King; there is no god but You. I am Your servant; I have wronged myself and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me all my sins; none forgives sins except You. Guide me to the best of character; none guides to the best of it except You. And turn away from me its evil; none turns away its evil from me except You. Here I am, at Your service, and all good is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You. I am by You and to You. You are blessed and exalted. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You."
error: Added clause: the English has "You are my Lord", which is not in the Arabic text.

segments_en: There is no heart except that it is between two of the fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills, He sets it straight, and if He wills, He lets it deviate."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"O Establisher of hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion." He said:
"And the Scale is in the hand of the Most Merciful; He raises some people and lowers others until the Day of Resurrection."
error: يَا مُثَبِّتَ الْقُلُوبِ means "O Establisher (Firmly Fixer) of hearts", not "Turner of hearts". "Turner" translates مُقَلِّب, a different divine epithet, and it contradicts the plea to make hearts firm.

segments_en: That ʿUwaymir al-Anṣārī,
of Banū al-ʿAjlān, came to ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī.

And he narrated the ḥadīth like the ḥadīth of Mālik, and inserted into the ḥadīth the statement: And his separation from her afterward became the sunnah (established practice) for those who undergo mutual imprecation.
And he added in it: Sahl said: She was pregnant, and her son used to be called by his mother's name.
Then the practice continued that he inherits from her and she inherits from him what Allah prescribed for her.
error: سُنَّةً was mistranslated as 'a year'. It means the established practice (sunnah), and 'بَعْدُ' means 'afterward', not 'after a year'.

segments_en: I used to serve al-Zubayr with the household chores. He had a horse, and I used to look after it. No chore was harder on me than looking after the horse: I would cut grass for it, tend to it, and care for it.
He said: Then she [Asmāʾ] received a servant: captives were brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he gave her a servant.

She said: Caring for the horse was taken off me, as [the servant] relieved me of its burden. Then a man came to me and said, "O Umm ʿAbdillāh, I am a poor man and wish to sell in the shade of your house."

She said, "If I give you permission, al-Zubayr may refuse that, so come and ask me while al-Zubayr is present." So he came and said, "O Umm ʿAbdillāh, I am a poor man and wish to sell in the shade of your house."

She said, "You have nothing in Medina but my house." Al-Zubayr said to her, "What is it to you to prevent a poor man from selling?" So he used to sell until he earned [enough]. Then I sold him the servant girl, and al-Zubayr came in to me while her price was in my lap.
He said, "Give it to me."
She said, "I have given it away in charity."
error: Segment 2: the translation wrongly identifies the one who received the servant as "Asmāʾ's mother's household"; it was Asmāʾ herself, whom the Prophet ﷺ gave a servant.

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he laughed and said:
"Do you know why I am laughing?"
We said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said:
"[I am laughing] at the servant's address to his Lord. He will say: 'My Lord, did You not protect me from wrongdoing?' He will say: 'Yes.'

Then he will say: 'I will permit no witness against myself except one from myself.' [Allah] will say: 'Today you yourself suffice as a witness against you, and the noble scribes as witnesses.' Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will be told: 'Speak.'
So they will speak of his deeds. Then he will be released to speak, and he will say: 'Away with you, and be gone!
It was on your behalf that I was arguing.'"
error: Segment 6 adds a clause not in its Arabic ('It was for your sake that I was fighting'), which duplicates segment 7 and mistranslates أُنَاضِلُ as fighting. That clause belongs only in segment 7, as 'arguing'.

segments_en: I saw Ibn Waʿlah as-Sabaʾī wearing a fur garment, and I touched it. He said: Why do you touch it? I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās; I said: We are in the West, and with us are Berbers and Zoroastrians. We are brought a ram that they have slaughtered, though we do not eat their slaughtered animals, and they bring us waterskins in which they put fat.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: We asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he said: "Its tanning is its purification."
error: The translation adds the first name "ʿAlī" to Ibn Waʿlah. The Arabic gives only "Ibn Waʿlah as-Sabaʾī", so this names a different person.

segments_en: The brother of Wahb ibn Munabbih said: This is what Abū Hurayrah narrated to us from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Then he mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The prayer of any one of you is not accepted when he has broken his wudūʾ until he performs ablution."
error: The Arabic says the narrator is the brother of Wahb ibn Munabbih. The translation makes Wahb himself the speaker and calls him "my brother".

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no prophet who does not have two ministers from the people of the heavens and two ministers from the people of the earth. As for my two ministers from the people of the heavens, they are Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl; and as for my two ministers from the people of the earth, they are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar."
This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth.
Abū al-Jaḥḥāf's name is Dāwūd ibn Abī ʿAwf.
It is also narrated from Sufyān al-Thawrī.
error: Passive 'yurwā ʿan' (it is narrated from Sufyān al-Thawrī) was mistranslated as active 'He also narrates from Sufyān', reversing who narrates from whom.

segments_en: I came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he said to me, "The first charity that brightened the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the faces of his Companions was the charity of Ṭayyiʾ, which you brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
error: جِئْتَ بِهَا means 'you brought it' (addressed to the narrator), not 'I brought'; the wrong person is made the one who brought the charity.

segments_en: A woman
entered upon ʿĀʾishah with a staff in her hand and said, "What is this?" She said, "This is for the gecko, because the Prophet of Allah ﷺ told us:
'There was nothing that did not try to extinguish the fire on Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, except this creature.'
So he commanded us to kill it, and he forbade killing snakes, except the one with two stripes and the tailless one, for those two destroy eyesight and cause miscarriage."
error: The Arabic says every creature extinguished the fire on Ibrāhīm except the gecko. The English said the gecko was the only thing that fanned the fire, which reverses who did what and what the general rule was.

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He went out dragging his garment in alarm until he came to the mosque, and he kept praying with us until the eclipse cleared. When it had cleared, he said:

"Some people claim that the sun and the moon are eclipsed only because of the death of one of the great men. It is not so. The sun and the moon are not eclipsed for the death or life of anyone, but they are two signs among the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, manifests Himself to something of His creation, it humbles itself before Him. So when you see that, pray as you would pray the most recent obligatory prayer you have prayed."
error: Subject and object reversed: Allah manifests Himself to a part of creation, which then humbles itself; the translation says something of creation is manifested to Allah.

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when ʿAmr ibn Qurrah came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, Allah has decreed wretchedness for me, and I do not see myself being provided for except from my tambourine struck with the palm of my hand. So permit me to sing, without any indecency."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I do not permit you, and there is no honor and no delight for you. You have lied, O enemy of Allah! Allah has provided you with good, lawful sustenance, yet you chose what Allah has forbidden you of His provision in place of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made lawful for you.

Had I warned you beforehand, I would have done such and such to you. Get up, leave me, and repent to Allah. But if you do it after this warning, I will beat you painfully, shave your head as a disgrace, banish you from your family, and make your belongings lawful plunder for the young men of Madinah."
So ʿAmr got up, with such evil and disgrace upon him as only Allah knows. When he turned away, the Prophet ﷺ said:

"These are the disobedient. Whoever among them dies without repentance, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will gather him on the Day of Resurrection as he was in the world: effeminate and naked, not covered from the people even by a thread, and every time he stands up he is thrown down."
error: Omits the tambourine (duff): the man's provision is from his tambourine struck with his palm, not generic earnings by hand.

segments_en: When the delegation of

Thaqīf came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he lodged them in the Mosque so that it would soften their hearts. They stipulated to him that they would not be conscripted, would not pay the tithe, and would not bow (in prayer). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"You shall not be conscripted and you shall not pay the tithe, but there is no good in a religion that has no bowing (rukūʿ)."
error: «ولا يجبوا» means they would not bow (in prayer), not 'would not be taxed'. The mistranslation hides the point of the Prophet's reply about rukūʿ.

segments_en: that he came to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās.
error: Wrong subject and object: the Arabic says he came to Ibn ʿAbbās, but the English says Ibn ʿAbbās came.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray his night prayer while she was lying across between him and the qiblah, asleep on the bed on which he slept, until, when he wished to pray the Witr, he would wake her and she would pray Witr.
error: Wrong subject: 'فَأَوْتَرَتْ' means she prayed Witr, not 'I'. Also 'الْفِرَاشِ الَّذِي يَرْقُدُ عَلَيْهِ' is the bed on which he (the Prophet) slept, not she.

segments_en: Among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ from Aslam: they used to pray Maghrib with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, then return to their families at the farthest edge of Madinah, shooting arrows and seeing where their arrows landed.
error: مِنْ أَسْلَمَ refers to the tribe of Aslam, not 'those who had accepted Islam', so the group of Companions was misidentified.

segments_en: The martyrs were mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:

"The earth does not dry from the blood of the martyr before his two wives hasten to him, like two nursing mothers who have lost their weaned young in an open stretch of land. In the hand of each of them is a garment better than the world and all that is in it."
error: ظِئْرَانِ means nursing mothers (foster-nurses), not gazelles; فَصِيلَيْهِمَا means their weaned young, not fawns.

segments_en: I was serving drink to Abū Ṭalḥah, Abū Dujānah, and Muʿādh ibn Jabal among a group of the Anṣār, when someone came in to us and said: "News has occurred: the prohibition of wine has been revealed."
So we poured it out that day, and it was a mixture of unripe dates and ripe dates.
Qatādah said: Anas ibn Mālik said: Wine was prohibited, and most of their wine at that time was a mixture of unripe dates and ripe dates.
error: فَكَفَأْنَاهَا means 'we overturned/poured it out', not 'that sufficed us'; the translation drops the act of pouring out the wine.

segments_en: with both hadith together: the hadith of Umm Salamah about kohl, and the hadith of Umm Salamah and another of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, except that Zaynab did not name her, similar to the hadith of Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar.
error: Zaynab is the subject (Zaynab did not name the other wife). The English wrongly makes her the one who did not name someone 'Zaynab'.

segments_en: A woman who served some of the daughters of the Prophet ﷺ reported that a daughter of the Prophet,
ﷺ, told her that the Prophet ﷺ used to teach her, saying:

"Say when you enter the morning: 'Glory be to Allah and with His praise; there is no power except with Allah; what Allah wills happens, and what He does not will does not happen. I know that Allah has power over all things, and that Allah encompasses all things in knowledge.' For whoever says these when he enters the morning will be protected until the evening, and whoever says them when he enters the evening will be protected until the morning."
error: Wrong subject: the narrator is a woman who served some of the Prophet's daughters, not one of the daughters serving.

segments_en: Abū Dharr used to say: Whoever says when he enters the morning: "O Allah, whatever oath I have sworn, or word I have spoken, or vow I have made, Your will is before all of that; what You will happens, and what You do not will does not happen. O Allah, forgive me and overlook it for me. O Allah, whomever You have invoked blessings upon, then upon him be my blessing, and whomever You have cursed, then upon him be my curse," he will be covered by an exception for that day, or he said: that day.
error: Wrong subject: in the supplication it is Allah ("You") who has blessed or cursed, not the speaker ("I").

segments_en: No one will enter Paradise who has an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart, and no one will enter the Fire"—meaning, one who has an atom's weight of faith in his heart."
A man said to him: "I like my clothes to be nice and my sandals to be nice." He said: "
Indeed Allah loves beauty. But arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people."
error: Added clause: the Arabic says only that Allah loves beauty (إن الله يحب الجمال); "Allah is beautiful" is not in the text.

segments_en: The hadith of one of them has entered into the hadith of the other, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir, from Yaḥyā ibn Jābir aṭ-Ṭāʾī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from his father Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān al-Kilābī, who said: One morning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the Dajjāl, sometimes lowering his voice about him and sometimes raising it, until we thought he was among the cluster of date palms.
He said: We left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then returned to him, and he noticed that in us and said, "What is the matter with you?"
He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, this morning you mentioned the Dajjāl, lowering your voice about him and raising it, until we thought he was among the cluster of date palms." He said,

"Something other than the Dajjāl is what I fear more for you. If he emerges while I am among you, I will contend with him on your behalf; and if he emerges while I am not among you, then each man must contend for himself, and Allah is my successor over every Muslim. He is a young man with tightly curled hair and one eye protruding, resembling ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Qaṭan. Whoever among you sees him, let him recite the opening verses of Sūrat al-Kahf." He said, "He will emerge between Syria and Iraq and will spread corruption to the right and to the left. O servants of Allah, remain steadfast!"
He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, how long will he remain on the earth?" He said,
"Forty days: a day like a year, a day like a month, a day like a week, and the rest of his days like your days."
He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, regarding that day which is like a year, will the prayer of one day suffice for us in it?" He said,
"No, but estimate its length [and pray accordingly]."
He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, how fast will he travel through the earth?" He said,

"Like rain driven by the wind behind it. He will come to a people and call them, and they will deny him and reject his words; so he will leave them, and their wealth will follow him, and by morning they will have nothing in their hands. Then he will come to another people and call them, and they will respond to him and believe him. He will command the sky to rain, and it will rain; and he will command the earth to grow, and it will grow. Their grazing livestock will come back to them in the evening with humps taller than ever, udders full of milk, and flanks stretched [with fullness]. Then he will come to a ruin and say to it, 'Bring forth your treasures,' and its treasures will follow him like swarms of bees. Then he will call a man brimming with youth, strike him with the sword and cut him into two pieces, then call him, and he will come forward, his face beaming and laughing. While he is in that state, ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, will descend at the white minaret in the east of Damascus, wearing two garments dyed with saffron, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, drops fall from it, and when he raises it, beads like pearls cascade from it. No one can smell his breath without dying, and his breath reaches as far as his sight. He will pursue him until he catches him at the gate of Ludd and kills him. Then he will remain so for as long as Allah wills."
He said: Then Allah will reveal to him, 'I have brought forth servants of Mine whom no one has the power to fight; so take My servants safely to aṭ-Ṭūr.'
He said: And Allah will send Yājūj and Mājūj, and they are as Allah said:
"They descend from every elevation."

He said: The first of them will pass by Lake Tiberias and drink what is in it. Then the last of them will pass by it and say, 'There was once water here.' Then they will travel until they reach the mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis and say, 'We have killed those on earth; come, let us kill those in the sky.'

They will shoot their arrows toward the sky, and Allah will return their arrows to them stained red with blood. ʿĪsā ibn Maryam and his companions will be besieged until the head of an ox will be better for one of them than a hundred dinars are for one of you today.

He said: Then ʿĪsā ibn Maryam and his companions will turn to Allah in supplication. He said: Allah will send upon them worms in their necks, and by morning they will lie dead like the death of a single soul. He said: Then ʿĪsā and his companions will descend and find not a handspan of ground that is not filled with their rot, stench and blood. He said: Then ʿĪsā and his companions will turn to Allah in supplication, and Allah will send birds like the necks of Bactrian camels. He said: They will carry them and throw them into al-Mahbil. And the Muslims will burn their bows, arrows and quivers as fuel for seven years. He said: Then Allah will send rain upon them that no house of hair or clay will keep out. He said: It will wash the earth and leave it like a smooth mirror. He said: Then the earth will be told, 'Bring forth your fruit and restore your blessing.'

On that day a group of people will eat from a single pomegranate and shelter beneath its rind. Milk will be blessed, so that a large group of people will be satisfied with one milch camel, a tribe with one milch cow, and a clan with one milch sheep. While they are like that, Allah will send a wind that will take the soul of every believer, and the rest of the people will remain, copulating openly like donkeys. Upon them the Hour will come."
error: Segment 10 adds Allah as the one sending down ʿĪsā and inserts 'disbeliever' (Arabic: 'no one'); segment 16 renders the place name al-Mahbil as 'where Allah wills'.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any man who has a slave girl, and teaches her and teaches her well,
and disciplines her and disciplines her well,
then frees her and marries her, will have a double reward.
And any man from the People of the Book who believes in his prophet and believes in me will have a double reward.
And any slave who fulfills the right of his masters and the right of his Lord will have a double reward."
Al-Shaʿbī said: Take it without anything [in return]; a man used to travel to Medina for less than this.
And Abū Bakr said, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Abū Burdah, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ:
"He freed her, then gave her a dowry."
error: Segment 9: the past-tense verbs (أَعْتَقَهَا ثُمَّ أَصْدَقَهَا, 'he freed her, then gave her a dowry') were rendered as imperatives ('Free her, then give her a dowry'), turning a report into a command.

segments_en: I said to ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ make a bequest of anything?" He said: "No."
I said: "Then how did he command the Muslims to make bequests?" He said: "He bequeathed [adherence to] the Book of Allah."

Mālik said: Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif said: Al-Hudhayl ibn Shuraḥbīl said: "Abū Bakr was taking command over the designated successor (waṣī) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?! Abū Bakr wished he had found some covenant from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, even if he had to have his nose pierced with a nose-ring for it."
error: In segment 3, وصي (the designated legatee/successor of the Prophet) was translated as 'the bequest', which changes who Abū Bakr is said to rule over. Segment 2 also turned the active 'he commanded' into a passive that drops the Prophet as the one commanding.

segments_en: I said to al-Aswad, "Did you ask the Mother of the Believers about the containers in which it is disliked to prepare nabīdh?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade preparing nabīdh in."
She said, "He forbade us, the People of the House, from preparing nabīdh in gourds and in pitch-coated containers."
He said: I said to him, "Did she not mention the ḥantam and the jarr?" He said, "I only narrate to you what I heard. Should I narrate to you what I did not hear?"
error: Segment 4: the verb ذَكَرَتْ is feminine, so the subject is the Mother of the Believers ("Did she not mention"), not "you".

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to prostrate on seven parts, and he was forbidden to gather up the hair and clothing: on the hands, the knees, and the tips of the toes.
Sufyān said: Ibn Ṭāwus said to us, and he placed his hands on his forehead and passed them over his nose.
He said, "This counts as one." The wording is that of Muḥammad.
error: The passive 'nuhiya' (he was forbidden) was rendered as 'he forbade', which makes the Prophet the one who forbade. In segment 2, Ibn Ṭāwus is the one who performed the gesture, but the translation made it ambiguous.

segments_en: Whoever grants a man a lifetime grant, [saying] it is for him and his heirs, his statement has cut off his own right to it; it belongs to the one to whom it was granted and to his heirs.”
Except that Yaḥyā said at the beginning of his narration:
“Any man who is granted a lifetime grant, it is his and his heirs’.”
error: Segment 4: أُعْمِرَ is passive; the recipient is granted the lifetime grant. The translation made the man the grantor, which reverses who owns it.

segments_en: That he was present with ʿUmar when ʿAmmār said to him: We were in a detachment and became in a state of janābah,
and he said: He blew into them [his hands].
error: تَفَلَ is a past-tense verb describing what was done (he blew into his hands). The translation renders it as an imperative command, 'Blow into them'.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not beat the female servants of Allah."
Then ʿUmar came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the women have become bold against their husbands, so command that they be beaten."
So they were beaten, and many women went around visiting the family of Muḥammad ﷺ. When morning came, he said:
"Last night seventy women visited the family of Muḥammad, every woman complaining about her husband. Those are not the best among you."
error: In segment 3, ʿUmar's request "so command (that they be) beaten" is mistranslated as a statement that the Prophet permitted beating them. This drops ʿUmar's request and attributes an action to the Prophet that the Arabic does not state.

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said, "If I were in front of the Prophet ﷺ, I would see his armpits."
Ibn Muʿādh added: Lāḥiq said, "Do you not see that he is in prayer and cannot be in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" And Mūsā added: meaning, when he said the takbīr he raised his hands.
error: Wrong person: Abū Hurayrah said 'if I were' (kuntu), not 'if you were'.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lifted the curtain, with his head bandaged, during his illness in which he died, and said:

"O Allah, I have conveyed [the message]"—three times. "Nothing remains of the glad tidings of prophethood except the good dream, which a servant sees or which is seen for him. Indeed, I have been forbidden to recite [the Qurʾān] while bowing or prostrating. So when you bow, glorify your Lord, and when you prostrate, strive earnestly in supplication, for it is likely to be answered for you."
error: "اللهم قد بلغت" is a declaration ("I have conveyed"), but the translation turns it into a question ("have I conveyed?").

segments_en: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir led us in a prayer which he kept brief. Some of the people said to him, "You have made the prayer light," or, "You have made it brief."

He said, "Even so, I made supplications in it that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." When he got up, a man from the people followed him, and he was my father, though he referred to himself indirectly, and asked him about the supplication. Then he came and informed the people of it:

"O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive as long as You know life to be better for me, and cause me to die when You know death to be better for me. O Allah, I ask You for fear of You in the unseen and the seen; I ask You for the word of truth in contentment and anger; I ask You for moderation in poverty and wealth; I ask You for bliss that never ends; I ask You for a comfort of the eye that never ceases; I ask You for contentment after the decree; I ask You for the coolness of life after death; I ask You for the delight of looking upon Your Face and a longing to meet You, without any harmful hardship or misleading trial. O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of faith and make us guides who are rightly guided."
error: أَبِي means "my father", not the Companion Ubayy; the narrator is saying the man was his father.

segments_en: That he heard his father
saying at the end of the prayer:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief, poverty, and the punishment of the grave."
So I began to supplicate with them, and he said, "My son, where did you learn these words?" I said, "Father, I heard you supplicating with them at the end of the prayer, so I learned them from you."
He said, "Then keep to them, my son, for the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate with them at the end of the prayer."
error: The father asks where the son learned the words (أنى عُلّمتَ); the translation wrongly has him say he taught them.

segments_en: The brother of Wahb ibn Munabbih said: This is what Abū Hurayrah narrated to us, from Muḥammad,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"We are the last, yet the first on the Day of Resurrection, although they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them. This is their day which was made obligatory for them, but they differed about it, and Allah guided us to it. So in this they follow us: the Jews tomorrow, and the Christians the day after tomorrow."
error: أخي وهب بن منبه is 'the brother of Wahb ibn Munabbih' (the narrator, Hammam), not 'My brother Wahb ibn Munabbih'; the speaker was misidentified.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent Abū Bakr and commanded him to proclaim these words. Then he sent ʿAlī after him. While Abū Bakr was on the way, he heard the groaning of the camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, al-Qaswāʾ. Abū Bakr came out alarmed, thinking it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but it was ʿAlī. ʿAlī handed him the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Abū Bakr commanded ʿAlī to proclaim these words. So they set out and performed Hajj. Then ʿAlī stood during the days of Tashrīq and proclaimed: "The protection of Allah and His Messenger is withdrawn from every polytheist, so travel freely in the land for four months. After this year no polytheist is to perform Hajj, no one is to circumambulate the House naked, and none will enter Paradise except a believer." ʿAlī would make the proclamation, and when his voice grew hoarse, Abū Bakr would stand and proclaim it.
error: Wrong subject: 'wa amara ʿAliyyan' means Abū Bakr commanded ʿAlī; the translation attributes the command to the Prophet ﷺ.

segments_en: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah said: It reached us that Musaylimah the Liar came to Madinah,
and stayed in the house of Bint al-Ḥārith.
Married to him was the daughter of al-Ḥārith ibn Kurayz,
who was the mother of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿĀmir.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him, with Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās,
who is the one called the orator of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a stick.
He stood before him and spoke with him. Musaylimah said to him, "If you wish, you may clear the way for us to take charge of the matter,
and then make it ours after you." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Even if you asked me for this stick, I would not give it to you. And I see that you are the one about whom I was shown what I was shown.
And this is Thābit ibn Qays, and he will answer you on my behalf." Then the Prophet ﷺ left.
ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh said: I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās about the dream of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which he mentioned. Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was mentioned to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"While I was sleeping, I was shown that two bracelets of gold were placed in my hands, and I found them dreadful and disliked them.
Then I was permitted, so I blew on them and they flew away.
I interpreted them as two liars who would appear."
ʿUbaydullāh said: One of them is al-ʿAnsī, whom Fayrūz killed in Yemen,
and the other is Musaylimah the Liar.
error: Segment 7: Musaylimah's offer was to leave/clear the matter (the authority) to him and his people, then have it pass to them after the Prophet. "Leave the matter between us and you" misrepresents the proposal.

segments_en: Al-Kifl of the Children of Israel did not refrain from any sin. A woman came to him and he gave her sixty dinars so that he could have relations with her. When he sat before her as a man sits with his wife, she trembled and wept. He said, "What makes you weep? Did I force you?" She said, "No, but this is something I have never done, and only need drove me to it." He said, "You do this, and you have never done it before? Go, the money is yours."
And he said, "No, by Allah, I will never disobey Allah after this."
He died that night, and in the morning it was written on his door: 'Allah has forgiven al-Kifl.'"
error: Wrong subject: he says to the woman "you have never done it" (وما فعلتِه), not "I have never done it".

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, was brought a case of a woman who gave birth to a child claimed by three [men]—similar to it—without mentioning Yemen, nor the Prophet ﷺ, nor his statement about making [the men] content with the child.
error: "وَلَدَتْ مِنْ ثَلاَثٍ" refers to three men who had relations with her, not three months of pregnancy.

segments_en: and Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
he said: Muḥammad informed me,
who is the son of ʿAmr, from Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥarmalah,
from al-Ḥārith ibn Khufāf,
that he said: Khufāf ibn Īmāʾ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed, then raised his head and said:
"Ghifār, may Allah forgive them; Aslam, may Allah keep them safe; and ʿUṣayyah, who disobeyed Allah and His Messenger. O Allah, curse Banū Liḥyān, and curse Riʿl and Dhakwān."
Then he went down in prostration.
Khufāf said: So because of that, the cursing of the disbelievers was made [part of the prayer].
error: Segment 9: the passive 'juʿilat laʿnat al-kafarah' (the cursing of the disbelievers was instituted) was wrongly rendered as Khufāf himself acting ('I made cursing the disbelievers part of my prayer').

segments_en: Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr
sent him to al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, the nephew of Namir, to ask him about something

that Muʿāwiyah had seen him do in prayer. He said: I prayed the Friday prayer with him in the enclosure, and when I gave the salām I stood in my place and prayed. When he entered [his quarters], he sent for me and said, "Do not do again what you did. When you have prayed the Friday prayer, do not join it with another prayer until you speak or go out, for the Prophet of Allah ﷺ commanded that a prayer not be joined to another prayer until one has spoken or gone out."
error: Wrong subject: Muʿāwiyah saw al-Sāʾib do something in prayer; the translation says Muʿāwiyah did it.

segments_en: I was present with ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān when al-Walīd was brought to him; he had prayed the dawn prayer with two rakʿahs and then said, "Shall I give you more?" Two men testified against him. One of them, Ḥumrān, testified that he had drunk wine, and the other testified that he had seen him vomit. ʿUthmān said, "He would not have vomited unless he had drunk it." Then he said, "ʿAlī, get up and flog him."
ʿAlī said, "Get up, Ḥasan, and flog him."
Al-Ḥasan said, "Let the one who enjoys its comfort bear its burden," as if he was upset with him. So [ʿAlī] said, "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, get up and flog him."
So he flogged him while ʿAlī counted, until he reached forty, and [ʿAlī] said, "Stop."
Then he said, "The Prophet ﷺ flogged forty, Abū Bakr flogged forty, and ʿUmar eighty, and each is a sunnah, but this one is dearer to me."
ʿAlī ibn Ḥujr added in his narration: Ismāʿīl said, "I also heard the hadith of al-Dānāj from him, but I did not memorize it."
error: In segment 3, the speaker who tells ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar to flog is ʿAlī (who was upset with al-Ḥasan), not ʿUthmān.

segments_en: It is related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that on the night he was taken on the Night Journey he found a pleasant fragrance, and he said:
"O Jibrīl, what is this pleasant fragrance?" He said: "This is the fragrance of the grave of the hairdresser, her two children, and her husband.

He said: The beginning of that was that al-Khiḍr was from the nobles of the Children of Israel. His route passed by a monk in his hermitage, and the monk would look out at him and teach him Islam. When al-Khiḍr reached adulthood, his father married him to a woman. Al-Khiḍr taught her and took a pledge from her that she would not tell anyone about him. He did not approach women, so he divorced her. Then his father married him to another, and he taught her and took a pledge from her that she would not tell anyone about him. One of them kept it secret while the other disclosed it, so he left, fleeing, until he reached an island in the sea. Two men came to gather firewood and saw him. One of them kept it secret and the other disclosed it, saying: I have seen al-Khiḍr.

It was asked: Who saw him with you? He said: So-and-so. He was questioned and kept it secret. It was part of their religion that whoever lied was killed. He said: So the man who had kept the secret married the woman who had kept the secret. Then, while she was combing the hair of Pharaoh's daughter, the comb fell, and she said: May Pharaoh perish!
She told her father. The woman had two sons and a husband. He sent for them and tried to persuade the woman and her husband to give up their religion, but they refused. He said: I will kill you both.

They said: As a kindness to us, if you kill us, place us in one house. He did so. Then when the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, he found a pleasant fragrance and asked Jibrīl, who informed him."
error: Segment 4: the subject of 'married the woman who kept the secret' is the man who kept the secret (the woodcutter), not al-Khiḍr, who had fled to the island.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed the eclipse prayer, and he said: "
The Fire was brought close to me until I said: 'O my Lord,
[will] I be with them?' And there was a woman—I think he said—a cat was scratching her. He said: 'What is the matter with this one?' They said: 'She confined it until it died of hunger.'"
error: Subject and object reversed: the cat is scratching the woman (تخدشها هرة), not the woman being scratched by the cat.

segments_en: We used to sit with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the mosque, and when he stood up, we would stand. One day he stood up and we stood with him, until, when he reached the middle of the mosque, a man caught up with him and pulled him by his cloak from behind—and his cloak was coarse—so that it reddened his neck. He said: "O Muḥammad, load these two camels of mine for me, for you are not loading from your own wealth or from the wealth of your father."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No, and I seek Allah's forgiveness. I will not load anything for you until you allow retaliation against you for what you did by pulling my neck."
The Bedouin said: "No, by Allah, I will not allow retaliation against myself."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that three times, and each time the Bedouin said: "No, by Allah, I will not allow retaliation against myself."
When we heard the Bedouin's words, we hurried toward him, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to us and said:
"I insist that whoever hears my words not leave his place until he is permitted."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man among the people:
"O so-and-so, load one camel for him with barley and one camel with dates."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Go on your way."
error: Segment 5: the one repeating the refusal each time is the Bedouin (يقول), not the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; the translation's "he" attributes it to the wrong speaker.

segments_en: A woman came to me to buy dates, and I said, "There are better dates than these in the house."
She entered the house with me, and I reached for her and kissed her. Then I went to Abū Bakr and told him about it. He said, "Conceal yourself, repent, and tell no one."
But I could not bear it, so I went to ʿUmar and told him. He said, "Conceal yourself, repent, and tell no one."
Still I could not bear it, so I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him. He said to him: "
Did you betray a man who went out to fight in the cause of Allah, [by acting] with his family like this?"
[He felt so ashamed] that he wished he had not become Muslim until that very moment, until he thought he was one of the people of the Fire.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowered his head for a long time, until Allah revealed to him:
"Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early part of the night" up to His words: "a reminder for those who remember."
Abū al-Yusr said: I came to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to me. His Companions said, "Messenger of Allah, is this for him alone, or for people in general?" He said: "
Rather, for people in general."
