error: Segment 9 reverses the reciter and recipient: the Arabic says the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to Abū al-Yusr (عَلَيَّ), not that Abū al-Yusr recited it to the Messenger.

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ narrated to them about the night in which he was taken on the Night Journey:
"While I was in the Ḥaṭīm"—and perhaps he said, "in the Ḥijr"—"lying down,

someone came to me and split"—and he said, and I heard him say, "he split what is between this point and this point." I said to al-Jārūd, who was beside me, "What does he mean by that?" He said, "From the hollow of his throat to his pubic hair."
And I heard him say, "from his chest to his pubic hair." "Then he took out my heart.
Then a golden basin full of faith was brought to me,
and my heart was washed, then filled.
Then a mount was brought to me, smaller than a mule and bigger than a donkey, white."
Al-Jārūd said to him, "Was it the Burāq, O Abū Ḥamzah?" Anas said, "Yes.
It places its stride at the farthest reach of its sight." "I was mounted upon it,
and Jibrīl set off with me until he came to the lowest heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' Then it was opened. When I passed through,
there was Adam,
and he said, 'This is your father Adam; greet him.'
So I greeted him and he returned the greeting, then said, 'Welcome to the righteous son and the righteous prophet.'
Then he ascended until he came to the second heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'Welcome to him, how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' Then it was opened. When I passed through,
there were Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā,
who are maternal cousins. He said, 'This is Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā; greet them.' So I greeted them and they returned the greeting,
then they said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'
Then he ascended with me to the third heaven,
and asked for it to be opened. It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' Then it was opened.
When I passed through, there was Yūsuf.
He said, 'This is Yūsuf; greet him.'
So I greeted him and he returned the greeting,
then said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'
Then he ascended with me until he came to the fourth heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' Then it was opened.
When I reached Idrīs, he said, 'This is Idrīs; greet him.'
So I greeted him and he returned the greeting, then said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'
Then he ascended with me until he came to the fifth heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad ﷺ.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!'
When I passed through, there was Hārūn. He said, 'This is Hārūn; greet him.'
So I greeted him and he returned the greeting, then said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'
Then he ascended with me until he came to the sixth heaven and asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'Who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' When I passed through,
there was Mūsā. He said, 'This is Mūsā; greet him.'
So I greeted him and he returned the greeting, then said, 'Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet.'
When I went past him, he wept.
It was said to him, 'What makes you weep?' He said, 'I weep because a young man was sent after me,
and more of his nation will enter Paradise than of mine.'
Then he ascended with me to the seventh heaven, and Jibrīl asked for it to be opened.
It was said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'Jibrīl.'
It was said, 'And who is with you?' He said, 'Muḥammad.'
It was said, 'Was he sent for?' He said, 'Yes.'
He said, 'Welcome to him,
how excellent is the coming of the one who has come!' When I passed through,
there was Ibrāhīm. He said, 'This is your father; greet him.'
He said: So I greeted him,
and he returned the greeting and said, 'Welcome to the righteous son and the righteous prophet.'
Then the Lote Tree of the Furthest Limit was raised up for me,
and its fruits were like the jars of Hajar,
and its leaves were like the ears of elephants. He said, 'This is the Lote Tree of the Furthest Limit.'
And there were four rivers: two hidden and two visible.
I said, 'What are these two, O Jibrīl?' He said, 'As for the hidden ones,
they are two rivers in Paradise,
and as for the visible ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates.'
Then the Frequented House was raised up for me.
Then I was brought a vessel of wine,
a vessel of milk, and a vessel of honey. I took the milk,
and he said, 'This is the natural way, which you and your nation are upon.'
Then the prayers were made obligatory upon me: fifty prayers every day.
I returned and passed by Mūsā,
and he said, 'What were you commanded?' I said, 'I was commanded fifty prayers every day.'
He said, 'Your nation cannot bear fifty prayers every day,
and by Allah, I have tested people before you,
and I dealt with the Children of Israel with the utmost effort,
so return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction for your nation.' So I returned,
and He took ten away from me.
I returned to Mūsā and he said the same.
I returned and He took ten away from me.
I returned to Mūsā and he said the same.
I returned and He took ten away from me.
I returned to Mūsā and he said the same.
I returned and was commanded ten prayers every day.
I returned and he said the same.
I returned and was commanded five prayers every day.
I returned to Mūsā,
and he said, 'What were you commanded?' I said, 'I was commanded five prayers every day.'
He said, 'Your nation cannot bear five prayers every day,
and I have tested people before you,
and I dealt with the Children of Israel with the utmost effort,
so return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction for your nation.'
He said, 'I have asked my Lord until I feel shy,
but I am content and submit.'" He said: "When I passed on, a caller called out: 'I have established My obligation and lightened it for My servants.'"
error: Segment 6: "and returned" is added; the Arabic says only the heart was washed, then filled (ḥushiya).

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ led his Companions in the fear prayer (ṣalāt al-khawf). He bowed with all of them, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the row right behind him prostrated while the others stood. When he rose, those others prostrated by themselves two prostrations. Then the front row moved back until they stood in the place of the others, and the others moved forward until they stood in the place of the front row. The Prophet ﷺ then bowed with all of them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the row right behind him prostrated. When they raised their heads, the others prostrated two prostrations. So all of them bowed with the Prophet ﷺ, and one group prostrated by themselves two prostrations. The enemy was in the direction of the qiblah.
error: Mistranslation of 'when he rose, those (the others who had been standing) prostrated'. The English wrongly says those who had prostrated stood up, which adds a clause and confuses which group did what.

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and he wanted to relieve himself, so he said to me:
"Go to those two small palm trees."
Wakīʿ said: meaning small date palms.
Abū Bakr said: the short ones. [He said:]
Tell them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ orders you to come together."
So they came together, and he screened himself with them and relieved himself. Then he said to me:
"Go to them and tell them that each of you should return to its place."
I told them, and they returned.
error: Segment 4: 'al-Qiṣār' means 'the short ones' (a variant gloss on the palms, as said by Abū Bakr), not the name 'Abū Bakr al-Qaṣṣār'.

segments_en: A man from Ḥimyar killed a man from the enemy and wanted to take his spoils, but Khālid ibn al-Walīd, who was their commander, prevented him. So ʿAwf ibn Mālik came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and he said to Khālid:
"What prevented you from giving him his spoils?"
He said, "I considered it too much, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Hand it over to him."

Then Khālid passed by ʿAwf, pulled him by his cloak, and said, "Did I not fulfil for you what I mentioned to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard it and became angry, and he said:

"Do not give it to him, O Khālid! Do not give it to him, O Khālid! Will you not leave my commanders to me? Your example and theirs is that of a man who was entrusted with camels or sheep and tended them, then, when the time came to water them, he brought them to a trough and they began to drink from it. They drank its clear water and left its muddy dregs. So the clear part is for you, and the muddy part is for them."
error: Wrong subject in segment 4: it is Khālid who pulled ʿAwf's cloak and asked 'Did I not fulfil for you...', not ʿAwf pulling Khālid.

segments_en: Khalīfah said to me: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah,
from Abū al-ʿĀliyah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, among what he narrates from his Lord, that he said:
"It is not proper for any servant to say that he is better than Jonah son of Matta."
And he attributed him to his father.
error: Wrong subject: the one who said the statement is the Prophet ﷺ (narrating from his Lord), but the translation made the Lord the speaker ("who said").

segments_en: Regarding the saying of Allah, {And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans}, she said: It was revealed about a man who has an orphan girl under his guardianship, and he is her heir, and she has wealth but no one to dispute on her behalf. He does not give her in marriage because of her wealth, and so he harms her and treats her badly. So Allah said: {If you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans, then marry those women who seem good to you}. He means: what I have made lawful for you, and leave this one whom you harm.
error: فَلاَ يُنْكِحُهَا is causative: he does not give her in marriage to others, to keep her wealth. The translation says he does not marry her himself, which reverses the sense.

segments_en: He was ten years old when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah,
and he said: I served the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for ten years of his life,
and I was the most knowledgeable of the people about the matter of the ḥijāb when it was revealed,
and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb used to ask me about it.
The first thing revealed about it was on the occasion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consummating his marriage with Zaynab bint Jaḥsh.
The Prophet ﷺ was a bridegroom with her in the morning, so he invited the people,
and they ate some of the food and then left,
but a group of them remained with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and stayed long. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up and went out, and I went out with him so that they would leave.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked and I walked with him until he reached the threshold of ʿĀʾishah's room,
then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ thought that they had left, so he returned and I returned with him,
until he entered upon Zaynab, and there they were, still sitting, not having dispersed.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went back and I went back with him,
until he reached the threshold of ʿĀʾishah's room,
and he thought that they had left,
so he returned and I returned with him,
and there they had left.
Then the verse of the ḥijāb was revealed,
and he put a curtain between me and him.
error: Segment 17 has the passive أُنْزِلَ ("was revealed"). The translation renders it as an active "he revealed", which gives the wrong agent.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A man must not be in physical contact with a man, nor a woman with a woman, except a child with a parent."
He said: And he mentioned a third, but I forgot it.
error: The translation adds "in one garment" and renders yufḍiyanna as "lie with". Neither is in the Arabic, and both change the scope of the prohibition.

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: I would not pay blood money for anyone upon whom I carried out the prescribed punishment (if he died), except the drinker of wine, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not establish any fixed punishment for it; it is only something we ourselves set.
error: أَدِي (from ودى) means to pay blood money (diyah), not 'to grieve over'; the translation changes the meaning of the statement.

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "Then he returned to Khadījah, his heart trembling," and he related the hadith like the hadith of Yūnus and Maʿmar, but he did not mention the beginning of their narration, namely his words: "The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was started of revelation was the true dream."
And he followed Yūnus in the words: "By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you."
And he mentioned the words of Khadījah: "O son of my uncle, listen to your nephew."
error: Subject reversed in segment 2: the narrator concurred with Yūnus (وَتَابَعَ يُونُسَ), not Yūnus with him.

segments_en: In the pre-Islamic period we used to say, when a clan became numerous: the sons of so-and-so have become numerous.
error: أَمِرَ means 'became numerous' (increased in number), not 'became powerful'.

segments_en: It was said to him, "Ubnā."
He said, "We know better; it is Yubnā, in Palestine."
error: Place names mistranslated as verbs/vocative: أُبْنَى / يُبْنَى are the town of Ubnā/Yubnā in Palestine, not "Build [it]" or "my son".

segments_en: Ubayy was struck on the day of al-Aḥzāb in the main vein of his arm, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cauterized it.
error: The Arabic names the man struck as Ubayy. The translation says "My father", which gives the wrong identity and adds a relationship that is not in the text.

segments_en: The people
asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ until they pressed him with their questions. So one day he came out, ascended the pulpit, and said:
"Ask me. You will not ask me about anything except that I will make it clear to you."
When the people heard that, they fell silent and were fearful that some matter had come upon them.

Anas said: I began to look right and left, and every man had wrapped his head in his garment, weeping. Then a man from the mosque, who used to be quarreled with and was called by a name other than his father's, stood up and said: "O Prophet of Allah, who is my father?" He said: "Your father is Ḥudhāfah."

Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, stood up and said: "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad as Messenger. We seek refuge in Allah from the evil of trials."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have never seen a day like today in terms of good and evil. Paradise and the Fire were shown to me, and I saw them just beyond this wall."
error: In segment 5, 'كان يُلاحَى' means he was being quarreled with (disputed with over his lineage), not that he was accused of being a quarreler; the passive sense was reversed.

segments_en: On the day of Uḥud, sixty-four men of the Anṣār and six of the Muhājirūn, among them Ḥamzah, were killed, and [the enemy] mutilated them. The Anṣār said, "If we ever get the better of them on a day like this, we will surpass them." He said: When it was the day of the conquest of Makkah, Allah revealed: "And if you retaliate, then retaliate with the equivalent of what you were afflicted with; but if you are patient, it is better for the patient." A man said, "There will be no Quraysh after today." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Hold back from the people, except four."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith from the narration of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
error: The man's statement 'لا قريش بعد اليوم' means 'there will be no Quraysh after today' (they will be wiped out). The inserted '[harm to]' changes the meaning.

segments_en: They mentioned their negligence in sleeping, and he said: They slept until the sun had risen.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no negligence in sleep; negligence is only in wakefulness. So if any of you forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, let him pray it when he remembers it, and [again] at its time on the next day."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Rabāḥ said: ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥusayn heard me while I was narrating
the hadith, and he said: Young man, be careful how you narrate, for I was a witness to this hadith with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: He (ʿImrān) did not object to anything in his narration.
error: Final segment: the subject is wrong. ʿImrān is the one who did not object to ʿAbdullāh's narration, but the translation makes the narrator speak in the first person ("I did not find...").

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās how the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was. He said:
I spent a night with him while he was at Maymūnah's,
He slept until, when a third of the night or half of it had passed, he woke up, went to a water skin containing water, and performed ablution, and I performed ablution with him,
Then he stood and I stood at his side, on his left, and he placed me on his right,
Then he put his hand on my head as if touching my ear, as if to rouse me, and prayed two light rakʿahs. I said:
He recited Umm al-Qurʾān (al-Fātiḥah) in each of them, in every rakʿah. Then he gave the salām, then prayed until he had prayed eleven rakʿahs including Witr,
Then he slept, and Bilāl came to him and said:
"The prayer, Messenger of Allah."
So he got up and prayed two rakʿahs,
Then he led the people in prayer.
error: Segment 6 is a declarative statement that he recited Umm al-Qurʾān in each rakʿah, but the English turned it into a question.

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, was passed by (a woman), with the same meaning as the narration of ʿUthmān.
He said: Do you not remember that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The pen is lifted from three: from the insane person whose mind is overcome until he recovers, from the sleeper until he wakes, and from the child until he reaches puberty?"
He said: You have spoken truly. He said: So he let her go free.
error: The passive مُرَّ عَلَى means someone passed by ʿAlī, not that ʿAlī passed by ʿUthmān. بِمَعْنَى عُثْمَانَ means the narration has the same meaning as ʿUthmān's report.

segments_en: He said to me: I see that you love sheep and keep them,
so take good care of them and wipe their nasal discharge,
for I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "
A time will come upon the people when the best property of a Muslim will be sheep,
which he follows to the peaks of the mountains or the mountain valleys, where the rain falls,
fleeing with his religion from trials."
error: رُعَامَهَا means the sheep's nasal mucus, not their pens.

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ in this hadith, he said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what if someone enters my house and stretches out his hand to kill me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Be like the two sons of Ādam."
And Yazīd recited: {If you should stretch out your hand toward me...} the verse.
error: كابنَي آدم is dual ("the two sons of Ādam"); the translation rendered it as singular "the son of Ādam".

segments_en: I had a forelock, and my mother said to me, "I will not cut it, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pull it and take hold of it."
error: The Arabic "لا أجزّها" is first person ("I will not cut it"), stating the mother's own decision. The translation turned it into a command to the narrator ("Do not cut it").

segments_en: I asked Jābir about the ḍabb (spiny-tailed lizard),
and he said, "Do not eat it."
And he found it distasteful. He said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: The Prophet ﷺ did not forbid it.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, benefits more than one person by it, and it is the food of most herdsmen. Had I had any, I would have eaten it.
error: لا تطعموه means "do not eat it"; "do not feed it to people" changes Jābir's statement.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to Umm Ayman, and I went with him. She handed him a vessel containing a drink. [Anas] said: I do not know whether she found him fasting or whether he did not want it. She began to protest loudly at him and to scold him.
error: Wrong subject: Umm Ayman handed him the vessel (not 'she was offered'), and she found him fasting (not 'he came upon her while fasting').

segments_en: From a member of the household of Umm Salamah, who said: The bed of the Prophet ﷺ was about the size of what a person is laid on in his grave, and the place of prayer was at his head.
error: The narrator is 'a member of the family of Umm Salamah' (آل أم سلمة), not Umm Salamah herself; the translation misattributes the report.

segments_en: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" He said, "
Do you have any difficulty in seeing the sun and the moon when the sky is clear?" We said, "No." He said, "
Then you will have no difficulty in seeing your Lord on that Day,
except as you have in seeing the two of them." Then he said, "A caller will call out: Let every people go to what they used to worship.
So the people of the cross will go with their cross,
and the people of idols with their idols,
and the people of every deity with their deity, until there remain only those who used to worship Allah, whether righteous or sinful,
and the last remnants of the People of the Book.
Then Hell will be brought forward, appearing like a mirage, and the Jews will be asked, 'What did you used to worship?' They will say, 'We used to worship ʿUzayr, the son of Allah.'
It will be said, 'You have lied; Allah never took a consort or a son. What do you want?' They will say, 'We want You to give us something to drink.'
It will be said, 'Drink,' and they will fall into Hell. Then the Christians will be asked, 'What did you used to worship?' They will say, 'We used to worship the Messiah, the son of Allah.'
It will be said, 'You have lied; Allah never took a consort or a son.
What do you want?' They will say, 'We want You to give us something to drink.' It will be said, 'Drink.'

They will fall [into Hell] until there remain only those who used to worship Allah, whether righteous or sinful. It will be said to them, 'What keeps you here when the people have gone?' They will say, 'We parted from them when we were in greater need of them than today, and we heard a caller calling out: Let every people join what they used to worship.
We are only waiting for our Lord.'" He said, "Then the Almighty will come to them.
He will say, 'I am your Lord.'
They will say, 'You are our Lord.'
None will speak to Him except the prophets. He will say, 'Is there a sign between you and Him by which you know Him?' They will say, 'The shin.'
Then He will uncover His shin, and every believer will prostrate to Him,
and there will remain those who used to prostrate to Allah for show and reputation.
They will go to prostrate, but their backs will become a single rigid plank.
Then the bridge will be brought and placed over the back of Hell."
We said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the bridge?" He said, "It is a slippery place where feet slide,
with hooks, clamps, and broad thorns,
having a curved thorn like those that grow in Najd, called as-Saʿdān.
The believer will cross it like the blink of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like the finest horses and riding camels.
Some will be saved unharmed, some will be saved but scratched, and some will be piled into the Fire of Hell,
until the last of them passes, dragged along.
You do not plead with me more earnestly for a right
that has become clear to you than the believers will plead with the Almighty on that Day
for their brothers, when they see that they themselves have been saved. They will say, 'Our Lord, our brothers used to pray with us, fast with us, and act with us.'
Allah the Exalted will say, 'Go, and bring out whoever you find with faith in his heart equal to the weight of a dinar.'
Allah will have forbidden the Fire to consume their forms,
so they will come to them, and some will have sunk into the Fire up to their feet and up to the middle of their shins,
and they will bring out those whom they recognize.
Then they will return, and He will say, 'Go, and bring out whoever you find with faith equal to half a dinar in his heart.'
They will bring out those whom they recognize.
Then they will return, and He will say, 'Go, and bring out whoever you find with faith equal to the weight of an atom in his heart.'
They will bring out those whom they recognize."
Abū Saʿīd said, "If you do not believe me, then recite: {Indeed, Allah does not wrong even by the weight of an atom, and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it.}" [The Prophet ﷺ said:] "
Then the prophets, the angels, and the believers will intercede, and the Almighty will say, 'My intercession remains.'
He will take a handful from the Fire and bring out people who have been burned,
and they will be thrown into a river at the entrances of Paradise called the Water of Life,
and they will sprout along its banks as a seed sprouts in the silt carried by a flood,
which you have seen beside a rock or beside a tree.
The part that faces the sun is green,
and the part that faces the shade is white,
and they will come out as if they were pearls.

Seals will be placed on their necks, and they will enter Paradise. The people of Paradise will say, 'These are the freed ones of the Most Merciful; He admitted them to Paradise without any deed they did or any good they sent ahead.'
It will be said to them, 'You have what you have seen, and the like of it with it.'"
error: Segment 32: 'an atom's weight of faith equal to a dinar' wrongly introduces an atom; the text says faith equal to the weight of a dinar (the atom tier comes later).

segments_en: "Two coats of armor"
error: جُنَّتَانِ (with ḍammah and shaddah) means two shields or coats of armor, not 'two gardens' (جَنَّتَانِ).

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is given a legal opinion without certainty, the sin of it falls upon the one who gave him the opinion."
error: Wrong subject: 'أُفْتِيَ' is passive, so the person is the one who was given the opinion, not the one who gives it. The translation reverses the roles of mufti and questioner.

segments_en: We used to speak about the Farewell Hajj while the Prophet ﷺ was among us,
and we did not know what the Farewell Hajj was.
Then he praised Allah and extolled Him, then mentioned the Antichrist (al-Masīḥ ad-Dajjāl) and spoke about him at length. He said:
"Allah did not send any prophet except that he warned his nation.
Nūḥ warned of him, and so did the prophets after him.
And indeed he will emerge among you.
Whatever is hidden from you about his affair, it is not hidden from you that your Lord is not like what is hidden from you" — three times.
"Indeed, your Lord is not one-eyed,
but he is one-eyed in the right eye,
as if his eye were a floating grape."
"Beware! Indeed, Allah has made your blood and your wealth sacred to you,
like the sacredness of this day of yours,
in this land of yours,
in this month of yours.
Have I conveyed [the message]?" They said, "Yes." He said, "O Allah, bear witness" — three times — "Woe to you," or he said, "Alas for you,
beware, do not return after me as disbelievers,
striking one another's necks."
error: Segments were not aligned (all text in segment 1). Also 'Nūḥ warned it' wrongly made the nation the object instead of warning of the Dajjāl, and the 'your Lord is not hidden' clause misstated the Arabic (your Lord is not like what is hidden/defective).

segments_en: With this story, he said: A man who had apostatized from Islam was brought to Abū Mūsā,
and he called him [to repent] for twenty nights or about that. Then Muʿādh came and called him, but he refused, so his neck was struck.
error: The Arabic verb is passive (his neck was struck). The English makes Abū Mūsā or Muʿādh the one who struck it.

segments_en: With this story, he said: He did not dismount until his neck was struck, and he did not ask him to repent.
error: The Arabic verb is passive (his neck was struck). The English makes Muʿādh the one who struck it.

segments_en: An insane woman who had committed adultery was brought to ʿUmar. He consulted some people about her, and ʿUmar ordered that she be stoned. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by her and said, "What is the matter with this woman?" They said, "She is an insane woman from the family of so-and-so who committed adultery, and ʿUmar has ordered that she be stoned."

He said: So he said, "Take her back." Then he went to ʿUmar and said, "O Commander of the Faithful, do you not know that the pen has been lifted from three: from the insane person until he recovers, from the sleeper until he wakes, and from the child until he reaches understanding?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "Then what is the matter with this woman being stoned?" He said, "Nothing." He said, "Then release her." He said: So he released her.
He said: And he began to say "Allāhu akbar."
error: The last clause of segment 3 is a narration (فَأَرْسَلَهَا, 'so he released her'). The English renders it as a second command, 'Release her.'

segments_en: The two sons of Busr al-Sulamī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered, and we placed beneath him a velvet cloth of ours, which we spread out for him, and he sat on it. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down revelation to him in our house. We presented him with butter and dates, and he ﷺ loved butter.
error: Narrators are the two sons of Busr al-Sulamī (dual 'qālā'), not Busr and his brother; the narrator identity is wrong.

segments_en: We came to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: Do you not marvel at Ibn az-Zubayr, who has risen up in this affair of his? I said: I will hold myself to account for him as I did not hold myself to account for Abū Bakr or ʿUmar,
though they were more deserving of every good than he,
and I said: He is the son of the paternal aunt of the Prophet ﷺ, and the son of az-Zubayr,
and the son of Abū Bakr,
and the nephew of Khadījah,
and the son of ʿĀʾishah's sister. Yet he holds himself above me and does not want that. I said: I did not think that I would offer this of myself and he would refuse it,
and I do not see that he wants good.
But if it must be so, that my cousins rule over me is dearer to me than that others rule over me.
error: Segment 4 mistranslated 'ابْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ' ('and the son of Abū Bakr') as 'the son of Abū Bakr's daughter's household', which changes the stated lineage.

segments_en: ʿAbd, who is Ibn ʿAbbād, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,

who said: Abū Ṭālib fell ill, so Quraysh came to him, and the Prophet ﷺ came too. Beside Abū Ṭālib there was room for one man [to sit]. Abū Jahl stood up to prevent him [from sitting there], and they complained about him to Abū Ṭālib. He [Abū Ṭālib] said, "O son of my brother, what do you want from your people?" He said:
"I want from them one word by which the Arabs will submit to them, and the non-Arabs will pay them the jizyah."
He said, "One word?" He said, "One word." He said:
"O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah." They said, "A single god?
We have not heard of this in the last religion; this is nothing but a fabrication." He said: Then the Qurʾān was revealed about them:
"Ṣād. By the Qurʾān containing the reminder. Rather, those who disbelieve are in pride and opposition," up to His saying:
"We have not heard of this in the last religion; this is nothing but a fabrication."
error: Wrong speaker: it was Abū Ṭālib who asked "O son of my brother, what do you want from your people?"; the translation made Quraysh the speakers.

segments_en: One whom I trust [told me]—and I thought he meant ʿĀʾishah—that she said: The sun was eclipsed during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he stood with the people in a very long standing. He stood with the people, then bowed, then stood, then bowed, then stood, then bowed; he prayed two rak'ahs, with three bowings in each rak'ah, bowing the third time, then he prostrated. So much so that some men that day fainted, to the point that buckets of water were poured over them, because of how long he had made them stand. When he bowed he would say: "Allah is the Greatest."
And when he raised his head:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him."
He did not leave until the sun had cleared. Then he stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said:

"The sun and the moon are not eclipsed for the death of anyone nor for his life, but they are two signs among the signs of Allah, with which He frightens you. So when they are eclipsed, hasten to the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until they clear."
error: أُصَدِّقُ means 'one whom I trust', not 'the most truthful'; also the rak'ah/bowing count is wrong: three bowings in each of two rak'ahs, not two bowings per rak'ah.

segments_en: O company of Qur'an reciters, stay upright, for you have been far outstripped. If you take to the right or to the left,
you will have gone far astray.
error: سُبِقْتُمْ is passive (you have been outstripped). The translation says 'you have taken a far lead', which reverses the meaning.

segments_en: I was sitting with ʿUthmān when he heard ʿAlī

making the talbiyah for ʿUmrah and Hajj. He said, "Were you not forbidden from this?" He said, "Yes, but I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ make the talbiyah for both together, so I would not abandon the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for your saying."
error: أَلَمْ تَكُنْ تُنْهَى is passive ("Were you not forbidden this?"). The translation made it active ("Did you not use to forbid this?"), which reverses who forbade whom.

segments_en: And Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Ibn Ḥujr said: Ismāʿīl informed us; and the other two said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
who is Ibn Jaʿfar, from Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Yazīd,
the freed slave of al-Munbaʿith, from Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, that a man
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a lost item that is found, and he said:
"Publicize it for a year, then learn its container and its binding. Then spend it. If its owner comes, give it to him."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about a stray sheep?" He said:
"Take it, for it is for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about a stray camel?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry until his cheeks turned red, or his face turned red, and then he said:
"What do you want with it? It has its hooves and its water-skin with it, until its owner finds it."
error: Segment 10 adds a clause not in the Arabic ("it will reach water and eat from trees"), and renders the pair in the wrong order.

segments_en: There is no ruqyah [treatment] except for the evil eye or a poisonous sting.
I mentioned this to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and he said: Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The nations were shown to me.
A prophet, and two prophets, passed by with a small group with them,
and another prophet had no one with him,
until a great multitude was shown to me.
I said: What is this? Is this my nation? It was said: This is Moses and his people.
Then it was said: Look at the horizon.
And there was a multitude filling the horizon.

Then it was said to me: Look here and there, in the regions of the sky. And there was a multitude that had filled the horizon. It was said: This is your nation, and seventy thousand of them will enter Paradise without reckoning."
Then he went inside and did not explain it to them, so the people began to discuss it and said: We are the ones who believed in Allah and followed His Messenger,
so we are they, or else our children who were born in Islam, for we were born in the time of ignorance.
When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he came out and said: "They are those who do not seek ruqyah, do not believe in bad omens,
and do not cauterize, and who put their trust in their Lord."
ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan said: Am I one of them, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "Yes."
Then another man stood up and said: Am I one of them? He said: "ʿUkkāshah has beaten you to it."
error: Segment 4: the Arabic says a prophet and two prophets passed with a group (al-rahṭ) with them; the translation wrongly turns this into another prophet with only 'one or two' followers.

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not mention "a driver with a good voice."
error: حَادٍ means a (camel) driver/chanter, not a person named Ḥammād; the translation invents a narrator's name and changes what was omitted.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Seek refuge with Allah from the Pit of Sorrow."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the Pit of Sorrow?" He said:
"A valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge four hundred times every day."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, who will enter it?" He said:
"It has been prepared for the reciters who show off with their deeds. And among the most hated of reciters to Allah are those who visit the rulers."
Al-Muḥāribī said: [the rulers who are] the unjust (al-jawarah).
error: In segment 7, the translation adds a gloss that al-jawrah means 'those who visit the rulers'. Al-Muḥāribī's word refers to the unjust rulers (al-umarāʾ al-jawarah), not to the visitors.

segments_en: My family sent me to Umm Salamah with a silver cup of water—and Isrāʾīl held three fingers together [to show its size]—in which was some of the hair of the Prophet ﷺ. When a person was afflicted by the evil eye or something else, he would send her his washing bowl [for water].
I looked into the container and saw some reddish hairs.
error: Omits 'من فضة' (of silver), a description of the cup.

segments_en: The three evil ones were mentioned in the presence of ʿIkrimah, and he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, having carried Qutham in front of him and al-Faḍl behind him,
or Qutham behind him
and al-Faḍl in front of him,
so which of them is the worse, or which of them is the better?
error: 'أَتَى' means he came, not 'was met'; the translation hides that the Prophet was the one carrying the boys.

segments_en: to ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr: "Bury me with my companions, and do not bury me with the Prophet ﷺ in the house,
for I dislike being held up as pure." And from Hishām, from his father: ʿUmar
sent word to ʿĀʾishah: "Permit me to be buried with my two companions." She said, "Yes, by Allah."
He said: Whenever any of the Companions sent a request to her, she would say, "No, by Allah, I will never prefer anyone over them."
error: Reversed object in ʿĀʾishah's statement: 'lā uthiruhum bi-aḥad' means she will never prefer anyone over them (the two companions), not prefer them over anyone.

segments_en: I said to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās: "O Abū al-ʿAbbās, I am amazed at the disagreement among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began the talbiyah, when he made the pilgrimage binding upon himself."

He said: "I am the most knowledgeable of people about that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed only one Hajj, and from that came their disagreement. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out intending Hajj, and when he had prayed his two rakʿahs in his mosque at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he made it binding upon himself while still in his place of sitting, and he pronounced the talbiyah for Hajj when he finished his two rakʿahs. Some people heard that from him, and I memorized it from him. Then he mounted, and when his camel rose up with him, he pronounced the talbiyah, and other people heard it from him. This was because people used to come in separate groups, so they heard him pronouncing the talbiyah when his camel rose up with him, and they said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only began the talbiyah when his camel rose up with him.' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on, and when he ascended the high ground of al-Baydāʾ, he pronounced the talbiyah, and other people heard that from him, and they said: 'He only began the talbiyah when he ascended the high ground of al-Baydāʾ.' By Allah, he made it binding upon himself at his place of prayer, and he pronounced the talbiyah when his camel rose up with him, and he pronounced the talbiyah when he ascended the high ground of al-Baydāʾ."
Saʿīd said: "So whoever follows the statement of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās should begin the talbiyah at his place of prayer when he has finished his two rakʿahs."
error: Wrong subject: "فحفظته عنه" means Ibn ʿAbbās ("I") memorized it from the Prophet, not that the people who heard it memorized it.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about the Stone:
"By Allah, Allah will raise it on the Day of Resurrection with two eyes with which it sees and a tongue with which it speaks, bearing witness for whoever touched it with right (in truth)."
error: بِحَقٍّ means 'with right/in truth'. The translation reversed it to 'without right' and made the Stone testify against the person, where it testifies in favour of the one who touched it rightfully.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Riders who are disliked will come to you. When they come to you, welcome them and let them be [free] to do what they seek. If they are just, it is for their own souls, and if they are unjust, it is against them. Satisfy them, for the completion of your zakāh is their satisfaction, and let them pray for you."
error: مُبَغَّضُونَ is passive (the riders are disliked or hated by the people). The translation reversed this to "riders who dislike you".

segments_en: A man fell ill and was cried over as if dead, so his neighbor came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said to him, "He has died." He said, "How do you know?"
He said, "I saw him."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"He has not died."
He said: So he went back, and the man was cried over again, then he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "He has died." The Prophet ﷺ said,
"He has not died."
Then he returned, and the man was cried over again, and his wife said, "Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tell him."
The man said, "O Allah, curse him."

He said: Then the man went and saw that he had killed himself with a broad-headed arrowhead that he had with him. So he went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him that he had died. He said, "How do you know?"
He said, "I saw him killing himself with the arrowheads he had." He said, "You saw him?" He said, "Yes." He said,
"Then I will not pray over him."
error: The Arabic "fuṣīḥa ʿalayhi" means he was wailed or cried over as if dead. The translation invents a man named Fasīḥ and has the neighbor go back to him.

segments_en: I said:
O Messenger of Allah, I have a slave girl whom I slapped.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarded that as a grave matter against me. I said: Should I not free her? He said: "Bring her to me." He said:
So I brought her. He said: "Where is Allah?" She said: In the heavens. He said: "Who am I?" She said:
You are the Messenger of Allah. He said:
"Free her, for she is a believer."
error: The Arabic says the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the matter seem grave to the speaker (ʿaẓẓama dhālika ʿalayya). The translation says it weighed heavily on the Messenger, which reverses who felt the weight.

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"When one of you marries his [female] servant to his slave or his hired worker, he should not look at what is below the navel and above the knee."
error: Roles reversed: the servant (khādim) is the woman being married to the man's slave or hired worker, not the male slave or worker being married to a female slave.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself taught me the call to prayer, and he said:

"Say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah"—twice each. Then he said: "Then go back and raise your voice: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; come to prayer, come to prayer; come to success, come to success; Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar; there is no god but Allah."
error: Subject and object reversed: the narrator was taught the adhan by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ personally, not the Messenger being taught.

segments_en: I used to hear Simāk ibn Ḥarb say, "One of the two sons of Umm Hāniʾ narrated to me." Then I met the better of the two, and his name was

Jaʿdah, and Umm Hāniʾ was his grandmother. He narrated to me from his grandmother that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon her and asked for a drink. He drank, then handed it to her and she drank. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, I was fasting."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"The one fasting voluntarily is the trustee of himself: if he wishes he fasts, and if he wishes he breaks his fast."
Shuʿbah said: I said to him, "Did you hear this from Umm Hāniʾ?" He said, "No. Abū Ṣāliḥ and our family informed me from Umm Hāniʾ."
Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated this hadith from Simāk ibn Ḥarb and said, "from Hārūn, the son of Umm Hāniʾ's daughter, from Umm Hāniʾ."
The narration of Shuʿbah is better.
Thus Maḥmūd ibn Ghaylān narrated to us from Abū Dāwūd, and he said, "the trustee of himself."
error: Segment 1: 'فَلَقِيتُ أَفْضَلَهُمَا' means 'I met the better of the two' (the narrator met the better one); the translation wrongly has the narrator say 'I am the better of the two' and 'I met [them]'.
